docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Internet Freedom Solution All you need for an unrestricted internet Hiddify – on your device

Hiddify is an easy-to-use VPN application available for iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Connect seamlessly to your HiddifyManager or any other VPN panel. Download it on mobile or desktop and enjoy unrestricted internet access.

HiddifyManager - to manage proxies and users

HiddifyManager simplifies setting up your own VPN server, allowing you to manage it even from your mobile device. Easily share proxies with family, friends, groups, or even hundreds of users.

Connect to the unrestricted internet easier than ever.
  • Easy to Use
  • Ad-Free, Secure and Open-Source
  • Offers advanced features such as support for IPv6, multiple subscription link types and more
  • Supports a wide range of proxy protocols including Hysteria2, TUIC, SSH, Reality, VMess, VLESS, Trojan and WireGuard, AmneziaWG, Naive, Psiphon, WebSocket, Quic, gRPC, http-split, httpupgrade, ECH, and Sing-box, V2ray, Clash and Xray configs, and many more
Read more about the Hiddify and see the source codes Free Testing Proxy - WARP Config Set up your own personal and dedicated VPN server.
  • Effortless Installation
  • One of the best VPN Servers for Iran, China, Russia, Brazil and the whole world
  • Multi-Core, Multi-Domain and Unified User Management
  • Supports a wide range of proxy protocols including Hysteria2, TUIC, Reality, VMess, VLESS, Trojan and Shadowsocks, WireGuard, AnyTLS, Snell, Naive, Mieru, xHTTP, httpupgrade, gRPC, WebSocket, ECH, DNS tunnels, Telegram proxy, with Xray and sing-box (hiddify-core) cores, and many more
Read more about the HiddifyManager and see the source code Install on server

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
How can I make sure that Hiddify is safe?

To make sure Hiddify is secure, you can take the following steps:

  1. Review the Source Code 🛠️ Since Hiddify is open-source, you can examine the code directly on GitHub for any security issues or concerns🔍. Reviewing the code yourself or consulting with a developer you trust is a good practice✅.

  2. Check Community Feedback and Contributions 🌐 The Hiddify GitHub page and repositories often have contributions, issue reports, and discussions from other developers and users👥. By reading these discussions, you can gain insights into the software’s security and any potential vulnerabilities that may have been addressed or raised by the community🛡️.

  3. Use the Latest Version 🔄 Ensure you’re using the latest version of Hiddify, as it may include security patches and improvements🔒. You can check the release notes on GitHub to see updates related to security📈.

  4. Follow Standard Security Practices 🔐 Using Hiddify in a secure environment involves applying good security practices, such as:

  5. Restricting access 🚫
  6. Regularly monitoring activity 📊

  7. Keeping both your operating system and Hiddify software up-to-date 🆙

  8. Transparency of Configuration 🌟 Hiddify Manager enables users to configure their own servers, providing complete control over proxy settings and data🔄. This transparency ensures that users can maintain secure configurations and modify them as needed🔄. Similarly, the Hiddify app offers users and developers the flexibility to customize and adjust settings, including proxy configurations and connection management, to meet their specific needs📶. Being open-source, the app allows visibility of any modifications or improvements, ensuring that users retain full control over their app experience while safeguarding security and privacy at every stage🔐.

By following these steps, you can be more confident in Hiddify’s security as a privacy and anti-censorship tool🛡️✨.

Which devices does Hiddify support?

Hiddify is designed to work across a range of devices and operating systems, covering both server-side and client-side needs🌐:

  1. Server-Side Compatibility (Hiddify Manager) 🖥️ Hiddify includes a server-side application, called Hiddify Manager, which installs on an Ubuntu server (Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 or 26.04). Hiddify Manager can be quickly set up with Cloud-init🚀, making it easy to deploy on popular cloud providers and datacenters🌩️. This server-side application manages configurations and connections for clients, offering a powerful backend for those seeking secure and stable internet access🔐.

  2. Client-Side Compatibility (Hiddify App) 📱 The Hiddify client-side application, simply called Hiddify, is versatile and supports all major operating systems, including:

  3. iOS 📲
  4. Android 🤖
  5. Windows 🪟
  6. Linux 🐧
  7. macOS 🍏

The development team is actively expanding compatibility to support additional device types, such as routers 📡 and 32-bit devices 🧩, to make Hiddify accessible to an even wider audience🔄.

With this structure, Hiddify provides a comprehensive solution for bypassing internet censorship and filtering, allowing users to set up servers independently and connect across multiple devices🔗, all while expanding accessibility on various platforms. 🌍

Is Hiddify free, ads-free, and open-source?

Yes, Hiddify is🌐:

  1. Free 💸 The Hiddify app is offered for free and has no subscription fees, especially for users worldwide who face internet filtering🌎. It allows users to quickly connect by importing proxies obtained from personal VPN servers (created by Hiddify Manager or any other VPN panel) or free services like Cloudflare WARP without any payment🔗. Additionally, Hiddify Manager is a free VPN server-building tool designed for non-commercial use⚙️.

  2. Ads-Free 🚫📢 Both the Hiddify app and Hiddify Manager are ads-free, providing a clean and distraction-free experience for users🧘‍♂️.

  3. Open-Source 🔓 Hiddify products are fully open-source, with the code available on GitHub. This transparency allows developers to review, contribute to, and customize the code, ensuring security and flexibility🔍.

These features make Hiddify a reliable and accessible tool for users seeking privacy and internet freedom without any cost or interruptions from ads🌈🔐.

How do I contact Hiddify’s support team?

To contact Hiddify’s support team, you can use the following channels📞🌐:

  1. GitHub Issues 🐞💻 For technical support or to report bugs, you can open an issue on the following GitHub repositories:
  2. Hiddify application Repository: github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app

  3. Hiddify Manager Repository: github.com/hiddify/hiddify-manager Opening an issue here allows the development team and the community to assist you directly🤝.

  4. Hiddify Website 🌐 Visit hiddify.com for additional contact information, resources, and documentation📚. The website also provides FAQs and updates to help with common questions🔄.

  5. Community Forums/Social Media 📲 You can also find support or ask questions in Hiddify’s community channels and social media:

  6. Hiddify Telegram Channel: https://t.me/hiddify
  7. Hiddify Support Group: https://t.me/hiddify_board
  8. Hiddify YouTube Channel: youtube.com/@hiddify
  9. Hiddify Instagram Page: instagram.com/hiddify_com
  10. Hiddify X Account (formerly Twitter): x.com/hiddify_com

These channels offer multiple ways to connect with the Hiddify support team and community members, keeping you informed about the latest updates and providing help when needed📢👥.

How can we support Hiddify?

  1. Financial Support 💸 You can support the Hiddify project financially to help with its development and continuation. For more information and to contribute, visit the Hiddify Financial Support page.

  2. Starring the Hiddify Project ⭐ By starring the Hiddify project, especially the repositories for Hiddify application and Hiddify Manager, you can help increase the project's visibility and credibility on GitHub.

  3. Contributing to Development 💻 If you have technical skills, you can contribute to the development of Hiddify. By helping to improve the code, adding new features, or fixing bugs, you can play an active role in the progress of this project. To contribute, simply visit the Hiddify GitHub.

  4. Giving a Five-Star Rating and Writing Reviews in Application Stores 🌟📱 By giving a five-star rating and writing reviews for the Hiddify app in various app stores, you can help increase its credibility and popularity, bringing it to the attention of more users. You can rate the app through the following links:

  5. App Store
  6. Google Play

  7. Microsoft Store

  8. Sharing and Raising Awareness 📢 By sharing Hiddify’s products, especially the Hiddify and Hiddify Manager, on social media and introducing them to people who need anti-censorship tools, you can help spread the project and increase its user base.

  9. Joining Social Channels and Groups 📲 By joining the Hiddify Telegram Channel and the Support Group, you can connect with other users and stay updated on the latest news and updates about the project. Also, follow the latest educational videos on the Hiddify YouTube Channel. Follow us on Instagram and X to stay informed about the latest project updates.

  10. Helping with Content Creation, Especially Video Content 🎥 You can help spread awareness and attract new users by creating educational and promotional content about Hiddify. Video content, such as tutorials on how to use and install Hiddify and highlighting its benefits, can be highly valuable for users. These videos can be shared on social media platforms and video-sharing sites like YouTube and Instagram to assist in better outreach and engagement.

  11. Providing Feedback and Reporting Issues 📝 By using the Hiddify app and submitting your feedback on the Hiddify repos, you can help improve the app's functionality and identify any issues.

docs.title: About Us
docs.text:
The Story of Hiddify Internet Freedom Solution

In Iran, internet access is heavily censored, even more so after Mahsa Amini's death and subsequent protests. Consequently, everyday individuals have faced restrictions in accessing the open internet since then.

The Hiddify project aims to provide people with straightforward and affordable ways to access the unrestricted internet on a broad scale.

Hidden Simplify Hiddify Timeline From beginning until now Sep 2022 First Working Version Dec 2022 Hiddify Manager v1 Provided 6 protocols Jun 2023 Hiddify Manager v7 Added Accounting Auto IP Selector Client apps for different OSs Documentation on Wiki Now Hiddify Manager v14 and Hiddify app v4

Working on the next versions

Our teams Development

Our developers bring our vision to life through Hiddify Manager and Hiddify app.

Design

Our designers create stunning visuals and improve the UX of Hiddify products through usability testing.

Content

We curate engaging and informative content including our comprehensive tutorials & YouTube tutorials.

User Support

We are always available to help answer your questions in our Telegram group.

Contributors needed

We are always looking for specialists to help make Hiddify better. Please send us your resume.

Email Us Development team

Join our dynamic development team! We're actively seeking Python, Kotlin, and Flutter developers to innovate with us. Shape the future of technology—let's build it together.

Content team

Are you skilled in creating captivating videos for YouTube, adept at video editing, and passionate about crafting visually stunning content for social channels? We want you to be part of our journey in redefining creativity.

Design team

Elevate user experiences with our design team! We're in search of a UX/UI design expert to play a pivotal role in enhancing user interactions across our diverse range of Hiddify products. If you have a keen eye for design, a passion for improving user journeys, and expertise in UX/UI, we want you to be a part of our creative force.

Want to support Hiddify?

The easiest way to support us is to click on the star (⭐) at the top of our GitHub page.

We also need financial support for our services. All of our activities are done voluntarily and financial support will be spent on the development of the project. To contribute, please visit our donation page.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text: This page explains what information Hiddify collects, what it does not collect, and how it is used.

docs.title: Summary:
docs.text:
Services provided by Hiddify are intended for use as is.

We do not gather any information from you. This app needs a private server from you, and we do not provide any server.

Crash data is sent via Sentry in the Hiddify app, without any sensitive data.

docs.title: VPN DATA
docs.text:
• We DO NOT collect or store any VPN data.
  • We DO NOT modify the contents of your VPN data.
  • We DO NOT share any sensitive or user-specific data with third parties.

This app is just a client app that users use to connect to their own servers. This means the app does not modify any VPN data, and users have complete control over, and liability for, their VPN data.

docs.title: 1.1 We do not Collect Sensitive Information
docs.text:
We do not gather, and do not even have access to, the following information:

  • Names (including subscriber names, usernames, and screen names)
  • Addresses (residential and business)
  • Telephone numbers
  • Payment details (credit card numbers, bank account info, billing records) We don’t store sensitive data.

No logs are collected on online activities such as:

  • Browsing history
  • Traffic destination
  • Data content
  • DNS queries

docs.title: 1.2 Data Collection
docs.text:
This app needs a private server from your side, and we do not provide any server. So we are not able to gather any information from you. Crash data is sent via Sentry in the Hiddify client app, without any sensitive data.

What information can be sent to your private server that is setup by you or any others? To add the server link in your client, you need a subscription link. With the subscription link your server can access:

  • Your IP address (as with any HTTP request, so be careful not to trust unknown servers)
  • Your Hiddify version

For your best experience, limited anonymous data can be collected on your server or any other server, after your explicit permission. It can include the following: - IP Address information of the Client - Operating System Version - App Version - Connection Status (TCP ping)

docs.title: 1.3 App Permissions
docs.text: The app does not need any permissions to access your phone’s contacts, location, device ID, storage, microphone, camera, etc. When you scan a QR code, the app may explicitly ask for camera permission.

docs.title: 2. Data Usage
docs.text:
Data is used for:

  • We do not collect any data, so we do not use it.
  • Crash data is sent via Sentry without any sensitive data.

docs.title: 3. Data Sharing and Transfer
docs.text: We do not share any data with any third parties. Crash data is sent via Sentry without any sensitive data.

docs.title: 4. Security Measures
docs.text: Strong security measures implemented to protect data. Staff access limited.

docs.title: 5. Data Retention
docs.text: We do not collect any data, so this does not apply to us.

docs.title: 6. Right to Be Forgotten
docs.text: We do not collect any data, so this does not apply to us.

docs.title: 7. Third Party Services
docs.text: Hiddify is designed to be used with your own deployed server. However, if you use third-party VPN services in our application, you should check their policies.

docs.title: 8. Advertising
docs.text: We do not have any advertising.

docs.title: 9. Children’s Privacy
docs.text: Parents are encouraged to teach children about online privacy.

docs.title: 10. Changes to This Privacy Policy
docs.text: We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. Thus, you are advised to review this page periodically for any changes. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page. These changes are effective immediately after they are posted on this page.

docs.text:
This app is developed for cases where there is no desktop, such as servers, and it supports all processors.

Full reference

HiddifyCli now has its own section: see Hiddify Core for run and srun, and the command-line reference for every command and flag.

docs.title: Download
docs.text: To download this app, go to here and download the file related to your processor.

docs.title: Execution of config or subscription link in HiddifyCli
docs.text:
To use it, the following command should be used.

HiddifyCli run -c <config file or sublink> -d <HiddifyApp config file or URL>
  • To connect to a specific configuration, just run the above command as follows.
HiddifyCli run -c <config file>

Here, put your desired configuration instead of <config file>.

  • You can also run a subscription in the app.
HiddifyCli run -c <sublink>

Put your subscription link here instead of <sublink>.

docs.title: Run config or subscription link in HiddifyCli with HiddifyApp settings
docs.text:
For this, you must first extract the settings related to your HiddifyApp.

  • To do this, open HiddifyApp and enter Config Options and click the three-dot menu.
  • Now click the Export Settings to Clipboard option to save the settings to the clipboard.

  • Now you can save these settings in a file with json extension.

  • You can also put these settings in Github and use its link as URL.

docs.title: Run config or subscription link in HiddifyCli with settings extracted from HiddifyApp
docs.text:
• Also, if you want to use your Hiddify app settings, you should use the following command.
HiddifyCli run -c <config file or sublink> -d <HiddifyApp config file>

Here, put your config file or sublink instead of <config file or sublink> and enter the configuration file related to HiddifyApp that you extracted in the previous step instead of <HiddifyApp config file>.

  • Instead of the config file, you can use the link related to the settings in HiddifyApp that you put on Github.
HiddifyCli run -c <config file or sublink> -d <HiddifyApp config URL>

Here, put your config file or sublink instead of <config file or sublink> and put the link of the desired settings in HiddifyApp instead of <HiddifyApp config URL>.

docs.title: How to Enable Free Internet Access for Clients Behind an OpenWrt Router Using HiddifyCli
docs.text: <markdown ="1">

docs.title: Enabling Free Internet Access for Clients Behind OpenWrt Router Using HiddifyCli
docs.text:
In another article, we explained how to download and install HiddifyCli on an OpenWrt router. In this article, we will guide you on enabling free internet access for the clients behind that router.

There are two main methods to allow clients behind the router to use free internet:

docs.title: ** Method 1. Using Proxy for Clients Behind OpenWrt Router**
docs.text: If you want devices connected to the router (like laptops, phones, and other devices) to use the proxy 127.0.0.1:12334, you can configure the following settings to make this proxy accessible as a central service for the entire network.

docs.title: 1.1 Enabling Port Forwarding on the Router
docs.text:
The proxy 127.0.0.1:12334 configured on the router is, by default, only accessible on the router itself. To allow clients to access it, the port must be opened on the router’s LAN interface.

  1. Add a NAT Rule:

You need to direct incoming traffic on this port to the proxy:

iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i br-lan -p tcp --dport 12334 -j DNAT --to-destination 127.0.0.1:12334
iptables -A FORWARD -i br-lan -p tcp --dport 12334 -j ACCEPT

Explanation:

  • br-lan: The LAN interface of the router.

  • 12334: HiddifyCli proxy port.

  • Save the Iptables Rules:

To save and apply the rules after every reboot, run the following command:

service firewall restart

docs.title: 1.2 Configuring Proxy Settings on Clients
docs.text:
Connected devices need to configure manual proxy settings. Follow these steps for different platforms:

  • Windows:
  • Go to Settings.
  • Navigate to Network & Internet > Proxy.
  • Under Manual proxy setup:
    • Set Address to the router's LAN IP (usually 192.168.1.1).
    • Set Port to 12334.

  • Save the settings.

  • Android:

  • Go to the Wi-Fi network settings.
  • Tap the connected network and select Modify Network or Advanced Settings.
  • Set Proxy to Manual:
    • Proxy hostname: LAN IP of the router (e.g., 192.168.1.1).
    • Proxy port: 12334.

  • Save the settings.

  • iOS:

  • Open Wi-Fi settings.
  • Tap the connected network and set Configure Proxy to Manual.
  • Enter the router IP in Server and 12334 as the Port.

  • Save the settings.

  • macOS:

  • Go to System Preferences > Network.
  • Select your current connection and click Advanced.
  • Under the Proxies tab, enable SOCKS Proxy:
    • SOCKS Proxy Server: Router IP (e.g., 192.168.1.1).
    • Port: 12334.
  • Save the settings.

docs.title: 1.3 Testing Client Connections
docs.text: To verify the proxy settings: - Open a web browser on the client device and attempt to access a website that is otherwise blocked without a proxy. - If successful, the configuration was applied correctly.

docs.title: 1.4 Additional Notes
docs.text:
• If clients need automatic proxy configuration, you can use a PAC (Proxy Auto-Configuration) file and specify it in client settings.

PAC File URL:

http://192.168.1.1/proxy.pac

The PAC file allows you to define routes and exceptions for using the proxy.

docs.title: ** Method 2. Routing All Traffic via Socks5 Proxy in OpenWrt**
docs.text: To route all internet traffic through Socks5 Proxy, you can use tools like redsocks or iptables. Follow these steps:

docs.title: 2.1 Install Required Tools
docs.text:
First, install the necessary tools. redsocks is used to route traffic through the Socks5 Proxy.

  1. Update Package List:
opkg update
  1. Install Redsocks and Additional Tools:
opkg install redsocks iptables-mod-nat-extra iptables-mod-tproxy

docs.title: 2.2 Configure Redsocks
docs.text:
Create a configuration file for redsocks at /etc/redsocks.conf:

nano /etc/redsocks.conf

Add the following content:

base {
log_debug = off;
log_info = on;
log = "syslog:daemon";
daemon = on;
user = "nobody";
group = "nogroup";
redirector = iptables;
}

redsocks {
local_ip = 127.0.0.1;
local_port = 12345; # Local port for proxy traffic
ip = 127.0.0.1;     # Socks5 server address
port = 12334;        # Socks5 server port
type = socks5;
}

Explanation: - local_ip and local_port: Redsocks listens here for traffic. - ip and port: Address and port of the Socks5 Proxy.

docs.title: 2.3 Iptables Rules for Traffic Routing
docs.text:
Create a script named redsocks-routing in /etc/init.d/:

touch /etc/init.d/redsocks-routing
chmod +x /etc/init.d/redsocks-routing

Add the following content to the script:

#!/bin/sh /etc/rc.common
START=99
STOP=10
start() {
iptables -t nat -N REDSOCKS
iptables -t nat -A REDSOCKS -d 0.0.0.0/8 -j RETURN
iptables -t nat -A REDSOCKS -d 127.0.0.0/8 -j RETURN
iptables -t nat -A REDSOCKS -d 192.168.0.0/16 -j RETURN
iptables -t nat -A REDSOCKS -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j RETURN
iptables -t nat -A REDSOCKS -p tcp -j REDIRECT --to-ports 12345
iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p tcp -j REDSOCKS
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp -j REDSOCKS
}
stop() {
iptables -t nat -F REDSOCKS
iptables -t nat -X REDSOCKS
}

Enable and start the script:

service redsocks-routing enable
service redsocks-routing start

docs.title: 2.4 Enable Redsocks
docs.text:
Enable and start redsocks:

service redsocks enable
service redsocks start

docs.title: 2.5 Reboot the Router
docs.text:
To apply the changes, reboot the router:

reboot

docs.title: 2.6 Verify Routing
docs.text:
Check if redsocks is working: - Check process status:

ps | grep redsocks
  • View system logs:
logread | grep redsocks

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
By following these configurations: 1. Proxy Method: Clients behind the router can manually use the proxy for free internet. 2. Routing Method: All TCP traffic from the router and connected clients is routed through the Socks5 Proxy.

For UDP traffic, additional tools like dns2socks or advanced redsocks settings may be required.

docs.title: How to contribute to this project
docs.text: For this, you just need to install git on your system.

docs.title: Install git on the system
docs.text:
Open one of the following based on your operating system.

Install git on Windows
  • First, go here and download the Windows version.

  • Then unzip the downloaded file and install it.

  • Then follow the installation wizard to the end with Next and Yes. It is recommended not to change the default settings.

  • By default, the installation location of git is in this path.

C:/Program Files/Git

  • It means that in the next stages, the projects will be placed in this direction. The work is done.

  • To check the version of git installed, open command prompt and run the following command.

git version
  • By default, git is installed in the user's Home folder.

Install git on Mac
  • First, go here and download the Mac version.
  • Then run it. It has a very simple installation.
  • After installation, to check the installed git version, open the terminal and run the following command. 
    git version

Install git on Linux

In most distributions of the Linux operating system, git is installed by default and you do not need to do anything special. But if you need to install it for any reason, you should search and find the appropriate command for that distribution. Next is the installation command related to the famous Ned distribution.

Debian/Ubuntu 

sudo apt-get install git-all

Fedora 

dnf install git-all

Arch 

pacman -Syu git-all

In all distributions, git is installed in the Home path of the user. - Run this command to check the version of git installed in the terminal. 

git version

docs.title: Using git to develop Hiddify app
docs.text:
• First you need to fork the project. For this, if you intend to fork the project, execute the following command.

git clone https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app.git
- Wait a while for the project files to be copied. - Now you have to create a branch of the project to work on it. To do this, first choose a name for the branch. For example, suppose we choose the branch name Hiddify-develop. Now run the following commands.

git branch Hiddify-develop
git checkout Hiddify-develop
- Now apply your desired changes to the files using any tool. It is recommended to use VSCode. - Do not forget that the path of all the files in the mentioned folders is in the installation stage. - Now, when you have applied your desired changes, you must also register the changes in git. Therefore, run the following commands in the terminal in order. - First, announce the changes to git with the following command.

git add
  • Then commit the changes. You need to provide an explanation for the changes here. 
    git commit -m "a short description of the change"
    For example, if the changes you are looking for are related to the core department, you can write such an explanation. 
    git commit -m "add some features to the core"

There is no problem if the explanations of this section are many, and by the way, it is recommended that the explanations be as complete and comprehensive as possible.

At this point, the changes have been successfully imported into the git system. Now you need to push the changes to GitHub. To do this, run the following command.

git push

Here, your GitHub account details will be asked. You need to enter your username and password on GitHub.

  • Now log in to your GitHub account and open the forked project. It has a path as follows:

https://github.com/<your_username>/hiddify-app

  • Now you will see a banner that informs you that your branch is one step ahead of the main project. To merge the changes with the main project, click Contribute and Open a pull request.
  • It's done, the changes have been sent to the project. Now, after the approval of the project manager, your changes will be added to the project.

The app is developed using Flutter and Go. For more information you can read through our Contribution Guidelines for development.

docs.title: How to install the Hiddify app
How to install the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to download and install Hiddify App on your phone or computer. Hiddify App is a free, ad-free and open-source client that connects you to a proxy or VPN server so you can reach the free internet. You need it if someone (or your own Hiddify server) gave you a config or subscription link.

Hiddify App is built on sing-box (the engine that makes the connections). It supports many protocols, including VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Reality, TUIC, Hysteria, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, Naive and SSH, and it accepts sing-box, V2ray, Clash and Clash Meta subscription links. See the full feature list on GitHub.

The latest stable version is v4.1.1.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Check that your device is supported:

Device What you need Android Android 7.0 or later iPhone / iPad iOS 15 or later Windows Windows 10 (version 1809) or Windows 11, 64-bit macOS macOS 10.15 (Catalina) or later, Intel or Apple Silicon Linux 64-bit (x64) Linux; Debian/Ubuntu-based systems are best supported

Windows 7, Windows 8 and RPM-based Linux

Hiddify App does not support Windows 7 or 8. There is also no .rpm package any more (it was removed in v4): on Fedora, openSUSE and similar systems, use the AppImage file.

docs.title: Which file should I download?
docs.text:
Pick the row for your device. Store versions update themselves; the files from GitHub do not.

Device Recommended Other options Android Google Play APK file: universal (works on every phone), arm64, arm7, x86_64 iPhone / iPad App Store — Windows Setup file (.exe) Microsoft Store, MSIX package, portable ZIP, winget macOS DMG file PKG installer, App Store (Apple Silicon Macs) Linux AppImage .deb package (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint), AppImage in a .tar.gz

All files are also listed on the GitHub releases page.

docs.title: Install the app
docs.text:
Open the section for your device.

Install on Android (click)

From Google Play (recommended)

  1. Open Hiddify on Google Play.
  2. Tap Install.
  3. When the install finishes, tap Open.

From an APK file (if you cannot use Google Play)

  1. Download the universal APK. It works on every Android phone.

  2. Open the downloaded file from your notifications or from the Downloads folder.

  3. If Android says it cannot install apps from this source, tap Settings, turn on Allow from this source, then go back.

  4. Android asks "Do you want to install this app?". Tap Install.

  5. When you see App installed, tap Open.

Install on iPhone or iPad (click)

  1. Open Hiddify Proxy & VPN on the App Store.
  2. Tap Get and confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your password.
  3. Open the app. The first time you connect, iOS asks to add a VPN configuration: tap Allow.

Note

The app is not available in the App Store of every country. If you cannot find it, your Apple ID may be set to a country where it is not offered.

Install on Windows (click)

You can also install from the Microsoft Store, or open Command Prompt and run:

winget install Hiddify.Next

(Hiddify.Next is the app's old name; it still installs the current Hiddify App.)

To install with the setup file:

  1. Download the setup file (Hiddify-Windows-Setup-x64.exe).

  2. Double-click the downloaded file. When Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.

  3. If a blue "Windows protected your PC" window appears, click More info.

  4. Click Run anyway.

  5. The installer shows where the app will be installed. Keep the default folder (or change it) and click Next.

  6. Choose extra options, such as a desktop shortcut or starting the app automatically, and click Next.

  7. Click Install.

  8. Wait while the app installs.

  9. When you see the window below, click Finish. The app starts. If it does not, double-click the Hiddify shortcut on your desktop.

If the app does not start

If Windows shows an error about a missing file such as MSVCP140.dll, install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64) and try again.

Install on macOS (click)

On a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) you can also install from the App Store.

To install with the DMG file:

  1. Download the DMG file (Hiddify-MacOS.dmg). It works on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.

  2. Open your Downloads folder and double-click the file.

  3. Drag the Hiddify icon onto the Applications folder. This copies the app to your Mac.

  4. Open Applications and double-click Hiddify.

  5. The first time, macOS may say it cannot open the app because it was not downloaded from the App Store. Click OK (or Done).

  6. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security (on older macOS: System Preferences > Security & Privacy > General), scroll down and click Open Anyway next to the Hiddify message.

  7. Click Open.

From now on, you can open Hiddify from Applications like any other app.

Install on Linux (click)

Option 1: AppImage (works on most 64-bit distributions)

  1. Download the AppImage file (Hiddify-Linux-x64-AppImage.AppImage). You do not need to extract it.

  2. Open a terminal and make the file executable. This example assumes the file is in your Downloads folder:

    chmod +x ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64-AppImage.AppImage

  3. Start the app:

    ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64-AppImage.AppImage

    You can also double-click the file in your file manager.

If nothing happens or you see an error about FUSE (a system library that AppImage files need), install it in a terminal and try again.

On Ubuntu 22.04:

sudo apt install libfuse2

On Ubuntu 24.04 and newer:

sudo apt install libfuse2t64

Option 2: .deb package (Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint)

  1. Download the .deb package (Hiddify-Debian-x64.deb).

  2. In a terminal, run:

    sudo apt install ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Debian-x64.deb

  3. Open Hiddify from your applications menu.

docs.title: First start
docs.text:
The first time you open the app, a welcome screen with three options opens. The app picks the language and region for you. If they are right, just tap Start.

  1. Language: if the app's language is wrong, tap Language and choose yours.
  2. Region: tap Region and choose the country you are in (for example Iran (ir)). The app uses this to open local websites directly, without the proxy. If your country is not in the list, choose Other.
  3. Turn on analytics: this switch is on by default. While it is on, the app sends anonymous crash and usage data that helps the developers improve it. Turn it off if you do not want that.
  4. Tap Start.

You should now see the app's home page. Next time you open the app, it goes straight to this page. The + button at the top adds a config or subscription link, and the big button in the middle (Tap to connect) connects you.

Note

The Android screenshots on this page come from version 5 of the app (a pre-release). On other versions and on computers the steps are the same, but some screens may look a little different.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: To add your config or subscription link and connect, read How to use the Hiddify app.

docs.title: How to use the Hiddify app
How to use the Hiddify app
docs.text: This page shows you how to add your connection link to Hiddify App, connect, pick a server and change the most useful settings. It is for anyone who has installed the app and received a link from their provider or from their own Hiddify server.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  1. Hiddify App installed on your device. If you have not installed it yet, follow How to install the Hiddify app.
  2. A connection link from your provider. This is usually your user page link (a personal web page that a Hiddify panel makes for each user) or a subscription link.

A few words you will see on this page:

  • Profile: one connection link saved in the app. A profile can contain many servers.
  • Subscription link: a link that gives the app a list of servers and updates it automatically. It must start with https://; the app no longer accepts plain http:// subscription links.
  • Config: the settings for one single server, for example a link that starts with vless:// or vmess://.
  • Proxy: one server in your profile that your traffic can go through.

Note

The screenshots on this page come from an older version of the app. The steps are the same in v4.1.1, but some screens look different.

docs.title: Add a profile to the app
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link (you got it from your provider or panel admin).

  2. On the user page, tap the button that opens your profile in Hiddify (in older panels: Tap to Start Anti-Filter). The app opens and adds your profile.

    1. If the app does not open by itself, the page below appears. Tap Copy Link to copy your profile link.

    2. Open Hiddify App. On the Home page, tap the + button at the top of the screen. The "Add profile" window opens.

    3. Add the copied link in one of these ways:

      • Tap Clipboard. The app reads the link you copied and adds it.

      • Or tap Manually, type any name in Name, paste the link in URL, and tap Add.

      • Or, if the link is shown as a QR code, tap Scan QR and point your camera at it.

    When it worked, your profile appears at the top of the Home page. If you see "Invalid URL" or "Failed to add profile", check that you copied the whole link and that it starts with https://.

docs.title: Add a single config
docs.text:
Use this if you want to add only one server instead of a whole subscription.

  1. On your user page, tap All Configs.

  2. Find the config you want in the list and tap Copy.

  3. Open Hiddify App and tap the + button.

  4. Tap Clipboard. The config is added to the app.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. After you add a profile, the Home page looks like this.

  2. Tap the big connect button in the middle of the screen. On Android and iOS, the first time, allow the app to create a VPN connection.

When the connection works, the button turns green and shows Connected. To disconnect, tap the button again.

If it stays on Connecting... or shows an error, try another server on the Proxies page (see below), or tap the update button on your profile to download a fresh server list. If nothing works, contact your provider.

docs.title: Manage profiles
docs.text:
• Update a profile: tap the update button on the profile card. This downloads the newest server list from your provider.

  • Switch to another profile: tap the profile card (View all profiles) and choose the profile you want.

  • Edit, share or delete a profile: open the menu of a profile in the list.

docs.title: Check and choose a server (Proxies)
docs.text:
1. Connect first, then open the Proxies page.

  2. You see every server in your profile, with its delay next to it. Delay is how long the server takes to answer, in milliseconds (ms): lower is faster.

  3. By default the app picks the fastest working server for you. To use a specific one, tap it.

  4. To measure the delay again, tap the Test delay button.

  5. To sort the list, tap the sort button and choose Default, Alphabetically, By delay or By usage.

docs.title: Quick settings
docs.text:
On the Home page, tap the sliders button at the top of the screen (next to +). From here you can:

  • Choose the service mode (see VPN mode on a computer below):
    • Proxy: the app only runs a local proxy. Other apps must be set up to use it.
    • System proxy (computers only): browsers and most apps use the proxy automatically. This is the default on computers.
    • VPN: all traffic of the device goes through the app. This is the default on phones.
  • Turn WARP on or off. See How to use WARP in the Hiddify app.

docs.title: General settings
docs.text:
Open Settings and then General. The most useful options are:

  • Language: the language of the app.
  • Theme mode: System default, Light mode, Dark mode or Black mode (fully black, which saves battery on some phone screens).
  • Start at login (computers): start the app when you log in.
  • Start minimized (computers): start the app hidden in the system tray (the small icons next to the clock) instead of opening its window.
  • Enable analytics: send anonymous crash reports to help the developers.
  • Disable battery optimization (Android): stops Android from closing the VPN in the background.

Other settings are grouped into Routing, DNS, Inbound, TLS tricks and WARP. Leave them at their defaults unless your provider tells you to change them.

Removed in v4

The old Config Options page, Enable TUN switch, Routing Assets (GeoIP/GeoSite), MultiPlexer (Mux) settings and the Experimental switches no longer exist in Hiddify App v4. Their useful parts moved into the sections above.

docs.title: VPN mode on a computer
docs.text:
On Windows, macOS and Linux, the app starts in System proxy mode. Some apps (for example games or some desktop programs) ignore the system proxy. To send all traffic through Hiddify, use VPN mode. (In older versions this was called "TUN mode".)

VPN mode needs administrator rights (called root on Linux and macOS). If the app shows "Missing privilege" or does not connect in VPN mode, first open the app with administrator rights:

Open the app as administrator on Windows

  1. If the app is open, close it completely: right-click the Hiddify icon in the system tray (next to the clock) and click Exit.

  2. Right-click the Hiddify icon on the desktop or in the Start menu and click Run as administrator.

  3. Click Yes when Windows asks for permission.

Open the app as administrator on macOS

  1. If the app is open, close it completely: click the Hiddify icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen and click Exit.
  2. Open the Terminal app.

  3. Run this command and type your Mac password when asked (the password does not show while you type):

    sudo /Applications/Hiddify.app/Contents/MacOS/Hiddify

Keep the Terminal window open while you use the app.

Open the app as root on Linux

  1. If the app is open, close it completely: right-click the Hiddify icon in the system tray and click Exit.

  2. Open a terminal and run the app with sudo. This example is for the AppImage in your Downloads folder; change the path if your file is somewhere else:

    sudo ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64-AppImage.AppImage

Then switch to VPN mode:

  1. On the Home page, open quick settings (the sliders button) and choose VPN. You can also go to Settings > Inbound > Service mode and choose VPN.

  2. Go back to Home and tap the connect button. When it turns green, all your traffic goes through Hiddify.

docs.title: How to use HiddifyCli on OpenWrt
docs.text: <markdown ="1">

docs.title: Complete Guide to Installing and Setting Up HiddifyCli on OpenWrt
docs.text: To install HiddifyCli on OpenWrt, follow all the steps below in order. This guide includes downloading, extracting, installing, and full configuration.

docs.title: 1. Download HiddifyCli File
docs.text:
To download the version suitable for your router’s architecture, use the following command for direct download: 

wget -O /tmp/HiddifyCli.tar.gz https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-core/releases/download/latest/hiddify-cli-linux-{ARCH}.tar.gz

Explanation:

  • Replace {ARCH} with your router’s architecture (e.g., mips, arm, or x86_64).

docs.title: 2. Extract the File
docs.text:
After downloading, extract the file using the following command: 

tar -xvzf /tmp/HiddifyCli.tar.gz -C /tmp

Command Explanation:

  • x- extracts the file.
  • v- displays extraction details.
  • z- opens gzip-compressed files.
  • f- specifies the file name.
  • /tmp/ is the extraction path (you can replace it with your preferred directory).

docs.title: 3. Move the Executable to the Appropriate Directory
docs.text:
Move the HiddifyCli executable file to /usr/bin/ using: 

mv /tmp/HiddifyCli /usr/bin/

docs.title: 4. Set Execution Permissions
docs.text:
To enable execution for the file, enter the following command: 

chmod +x /usr/bin/HiddifyCli

docs.title: 5. Create an Init Script
docs.text:
To create an automatic service: 1. Create a file named HiddifyCli in /etc/init.d/: 

touch /etc/init.d/HiddifyCli
  1. Fill the file with the following content: 
#!/bin/sh /etc/rc.common  
START=91  USE_PROCD=1  start_service() {  procd_open_instance  procd_set_param command /usr/bin/HiddifyCli run -c /root/config.conf  procd_set_param stdout 1  procd_set_param stderr 1  procd_set_param respawn  procd_close_instance  }
  1. Set the file permissions: 
chmod 755 /etc/init.d/HiddifyCli

docs.title: 6. Enable and Start the Service
docs.text:
Run the following commands to enable and start the service: 

service HiddifyCli enable  service HiddifyCli start

docs.title: 7. Configure the Settings
docs.text:
1. Extract the Configuration from Hiddify Desktop App:
  2. Set up your desired configurations in the app.
  3. Export the config and save it as a text file.

  4. Rename the file extension to .conf (e.g., config.conf).

  5. Move the Config File to /root/ on the Router: 

mv config.conf /root/

docs.title: 8. Reboot the Router
docs.text:
Restart the router to apply the changes: 

reboot

After rebooting, the HiddifyCli service will be active, and the Socks5 Proxy will be available at: 

127.0.0.1:12334

docs.title: Additional Notes:
docs.text:
• To check the router’s architecture, run the following command: 
uname -m
  • If any issues arise during the process, check the service logs using: 
logread | grep HiddifyCli

In another article, we will explain how to enable free internet access for clients behind the router.

docs.title: How to use UDP Turn Relay in HiddifyApp
How to use UDP Turn Relay
docs.text:
Recently, a feature called UDP Turn Relay is used in messengers to bypass filtering. That is, in this case, messengers are used as intermediate servers (relay) and traffic is sent to the main server through them. This can be used for messengers that are active inside Iran and support this protocol, or for foreign messengers that are not filtered. The diagram of free internet connection in this case is as follows.

Note that this feature only works for configurations that are on the UDP protocol. This means that this feature can be used on Hysteria2 or TUIC v5, but it cannot be used for reality.

To use it, just put the parameters of that messenger at the end of your config link according to the command below.

relay=urlencoded(turn://user:pass@host:port?realm=t)

Where user is the username to connect to the protocol in the desired messenger. pass is also the password for this account in that messenger. Also, host is the host-name for connecting to the messenger, and port is the port for connecting to the messenger. The realm parameter is related to the authentication area inside the host-name. That is, which area of the messenger can be authenticated with this account.

For example, in Bale messenger (an Iranian Messenger), these parameters are as follows.

relay=urlencoded(turn://balelivekit:GygZPHQSgAV7L5L8@meet-turn.bale.sh:443?realm=bale.ai)

First, you convert this information to UTF-8 using an Encoder. For example, you can use this Encoder, the output of which is as follows:

relay=turn%3A%2F%2Fbalelivekit%3AGygZPHQSgAV7L5L8%40meet-turn.bale.sh%3A443%3Frealm%3Dbale.ai

Now if we have a hysteria configuration based on UDP as follows:

hysteria2://87543215-15ac-54f6-3895-34e4e931f5b4@45.120.34.46:11464?hiddify=1&obfs=salamander&obfs-password=bdgf!huy678559j89GrTu&sni=www.speedtest.net&insecure=1#test

Finally, we add the encoded information related to the relay (messenger) at the end of the hysteria link. For this, we first put an & and copy the link exactly before # as below:

hysteria2://87543215-15ac-54f6-3895-34e4e931f5b4@45.120.34.46:11464?hiddify=1&obfs=salamander&obfs-password=bdgf!huy678559j89GrTu&sni=www.speedtest.net&insecure=1&relay=turn%3A%2F%2Fbalelivekit%3AGygZPHQSgAV7L5L8%40meet-turn.bale.sh%3A443%3Frealm%3Dbale.ai#test

You can import this link in the Hiddify-Next program and because this program supports the UDP Turn Relay protocol, you can use this feature.

NOTE!

Bale messenger disabled the said feature after a short time. Based on the contents explained above, you should find a messenger that supports this feature from the list of internal messengers of Iran or non-filtered external messengers.

docs.title: How to use WARP in the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page explains how to use Cloudflare WARP in Hiddify App: the easy way (one switch in the settings) and the advanced way (writing your own warp:// config). Use it if you want a free connection, or if you want to hide your proxy traffic behind WARP.

WARP is a free VPN service from Cloudflare. It is based on WireGuard, a fast and simple VPN protocol. Hiddify App can create a WARP account for you and add "noise" (extra fake packets) so that WARP traffic is harder for filters to detect and block.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Hiddify App: see How to install the Hiddify app.
  • For the advanced way, you should already know how to add a profile: see How to use the Hiddify app.

docs.title: The easy way: turn on WARP in the settings
docs.text:
1. Open Settings and then WARP.
  2. Turn on Enable WARP. Read the "Cloudflare WARP consent" message and tap Agree.
  3. Tap Generate WARP config. When it is done, the app shows "Warp config is generated".
  4. Choose a Detour mode:
    • Detour proxies through WARP ("Unblock proxies by WARP"): your proxy server is reached through WARP. Use this if your proxy server's IP is blocked.
    • Detour WARP through proxies ("Extra security by WARP"): you connect to your proxy first and then to WARP. Websites see a Cloudflare IP instead of your proxy's IP.
  5. Go back to Home and connect as usual. When it works, the connect button turns green.

You can also turn WARP on and off from the quick settings on the Home page (the sliders button at the top).

The other options on the WARP page are License key (a WARP+ key, if you have one), Clean IP and Port (which Cloudflare address to connect to; auto by default), and Noise count, Noise mode, Noise size and Noise delay. These four noise options work like the ifp, ifpm, ifps and ifpd parameters explained below.

Quick test

To try a ready-made WARP profile, open hiddify.com/warp on a device that has Hiddify App and tap the link there.

docs.title: The advanced way: write your own WARP config
docs.text: You can build a warp:// link yourself and add it to the app like any other config (copy it, then tap + and Clipboard). The parts of the link are explained below.

docs.title: Noise modes (ifpm)
docs.text:
There are 6 main modes and 2 advanced modes. Each one adds a fake header (noise) in front of WARP traffic to help it get past filtering.

  • m1: the header is random.
  • m2: the header is random and stays the same, with no trace of WireGuard or WARP in it.
  • m3: the header uses the QUIC protocol.
  • m4: the header uses QUIC and stays the same, with no trace of WireGuard or WARP in it.
  • m5: the header uses LQUIC.
  • m6: the header uses LQUIC and stays the same, with no trace of WireGuard or WARP in it.
  • h_HEX: an advanced mode. You choose the first byte of the fake packet as a hex number (from 00 to FF). For example, ifpm=h_30 makes every fake packet start with 0x30.
  • g_HEX_HEX…: an advanced mode. The app picks one of the hex bytes you list at random each time. For example, ifpm=g_10_20_30 uses 0x10, 0x20 or 0x30.

Tip

The recommended mode is m4. It is also the app's default.

docs.title: Number, size and delay of noise packets
docs.text:
Each of these is a range (min-max). Each time, the app picks a random value inside the range.

  • ifp: how many noise packets to send. For example, ifp=40-80 sends between 40 and 80 noise packets.
  • ifps: the size of each noise packet, in bytes. For example, ifps=40-100 makes each packet between 40 and 100 bytes.
  • ifpd: the delay between noise packets, in milliseconds. For example, ifpd=4-8 waits between 4 and 8 ms. Smaller delays usually work better.

docs.title: Which Cloudflare IP to use
docs.text:
• auto4: Cloudflare gives the config an IPv4 address automatically.
  • auto6: Cloudflare gives the config an IPv6 address automatically.
  • auto: Cloudflare can give either an IPv4 or an IPv6 address.
  • A clean IPv4 address: type it directly. For example: 188.114.97.170
  • A clean IPv6 address: put it inside []. For example: [2a01:4ef:f0:10a5::1]

A clean IP is a Cloudflare IP address that is not blocked on your network.

Tip

You can find clean IPs with a scanner, for example: CFScanner, Quick WARP on WARP, Ptechgithub WARP. These are community tools, not made by Hiddify.

docs.title: Name of the config
docs.text:
To give the config a name, add # and the name at the end. The name must be one word (no spaces). For example:

warp://auto#NAME

docs.title: WARP in WARP (WoW)
docs.text:
You can chain two WARP connections: you connect to the first WARP, and from there to the second one. Websites then see the IP of the second WARP. Add &&detour= after the first WARP config, followed by the second one. For example:

warp://auto&&detour=warp://auto

docs.title: Putting it all together
docs.text:
The general form of a WARP config is:

warp://License@IP:port?ifp=n1-n2&ifps=s1-s2&ifpd=d1-d2&ifpm=mode#name

Example:

warp://auto?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=m4#m4

This adds a WARP config named m4 to the app.

You can also chain two WARPs. For example:

warp://auto?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=m4#m4&&detour=warp://188.114.97.170:894?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=m3#m3

This adds a config named m4 that goes through a second WARP (WARP in WARP) named m3.

For more examples, see the official sample files warp and warp2.

Final tips

  • Use one of the scanners above to find a clean IP that works on your network, then build your config with the formula above.
  • If it does not connect, change the ranges (ifp, ifps, ifpd) or try another mode, and test again.

docs.title: Profile Title:
docs.text:
We use the first item from the following list if it is not empty or null

  • "Profile-Title" header
  • "content-disposition" header (described bellow)
  • URL Fragment (anything after # in the url)
  • the last part of the URL as the configuration file name. Any .txt .json .yaml or .yml will be removed

docs.title: Profile-Title
docs.text:
You can use base64 encoded UTF8 name for profile title that allows you to have emoji in profile title 😍 However you use also the ascii name in the header. Example:

Profile-Title: base64:SSDinaTvuI8gSGlkZGlmeQ==
It will show the profile title as I ❤️ Hiddify

Profile-Title: I love hiddify
It will show the profile title as I love Hiddify

docs.title: content-disposition
docs.text:
If the Profile-Title is not set for backward compatibility with clash configs we use the value corresponding to filename as the configuration file name, otherwise use the last part of the URL as the configuration file name. Any .txt, .yaml or .yml will be removed

content-disposition: attachment; filename="abc.txt"

docs.title: profile-update-interval
docs.text:
If there is a profile-update-interval field in the response header, the configuration file automatic update interval is set to the corresponding value, in hours

profile-update-interval: 12

docs.title: subscription-userinfo
docs.text:
If the subscription-userinfo field exists in the response header, its corresponding traffic and expiration information will be displayed in the Profiles module, specification reference here

subscription-userinfo: upload=455727941; download=6174315083; totl=1073741824000; expire=1671815872

docs.title: profile-web-page-url
docs.text: If the profile-web-page-url field exists in the response header, the Open web page option will be displayed in the profile, allowing the user to jump to the corresponding portal home page

docs.title: support-url
docs.text: If the support-url field exists in the response header, the support option will be displayed in the profile, allowing the user to jump to the corresponding portal home page

docs.title: moved-permanently-to
docs.text: If the moved-permanently-to field exists in the response header, this will update the subscription url. It is useful when your sublink is blocked or you want to change the domain.

docs.title: DNS
docs.text: If the DNS field exists in the response header, and the user did not set his/her own preferred DNS, the application will use this DNS server. (In the clash profile this setting can be override)

docs.title: Example
if you can not modify HTTP header (e g. In GitHub)
docs.text:
You can add headers in the first 10 lines of the file with skip characters such as // for json or # for Yaml and sub links

E.g.,

#profile-title: Hiddify
#profile-title: base64:base64string
#profile-update-interval: 1
#subscription-userinfo: upload=455727941; download=6174315083; total=1073741824000; expire=1671815872
#support-url: https://t.me/hiddify
#profile-web-page-url: https://hiddify.com

docs.title: Fragment Parameters
docs.text:
If you want to use Fragment in your links, you have to consider the following parameters 

&fragment=size,sleep,hellotls

For example, you just need to put the following information in your links

&fragment=10-100,100-200,hellotls

docs.title: MUX parameter
docs.text:
If you want to setup Mux parameters in your link

mux : "smux/h2mux/yamux"
mux_max : "number" e.g. 6
mux_min : "number" e.g. 2
mux_pad : "true/false"
mux_down : "number in mbps" e.g. 100
mux_up : "number in mbps" e.g. 200

Here:

  • mux can be one of smux, yamux, h2mux

  • mux_max is the maximum number of connections.

  • mux_min is the minimum number of streams.

  • mux_pad is a true or false parameter which turns on or off this feature on MUX. It Should be the same with the server.

  • mux_down is the download bandwidth for MUX in mbps.

  • mux_up is the upload bandwidth for MUX in mbps.

Example: mux=smux&mux_max=4&mux_min=0&mix_pad=false&mux_up=10&mux_down=10

docs.title: The Story of Hiddify…
docs.text:
Hello to all Hiddify supporters,

Around this time last year, we were all in shock, and everyone was trying to help in any way they could.

Many of our loved ones gave their lives, and their absence will always be felt in our hearts.

Many lost their eyesight, others were fired, some were imprisoned, and more…

All of this happened as part of protests for their natural rights.

These events will never be erased from our minds and will always bring pain to our hearts.

It was during these difficult days last year that we decided to do what we could by providing simple access to the internet, making it easier for the dear people of our country. That was the beginning of this project, and Hiddify was born during these very days.

In the first days, we tried to review various censorship methods and create a list of VPS providers.

After that, we created extremely easy and free installations for Microsoft Azure.

We expanded the project to other datacenters, including quick installations for Hetzner, Oracle Cloud, and OVH. The goal was for everyone to be able to set up their own server without any technical knowledge.

Then, we developed the initial version of the Hiddify server and tried to teach the activation process for the client in a simple way. We also worked to ensure that the server app was resistant to VPN detection bots, obtained valid certificates, set safety configurations, and applied appropriate settings.

As time passed and the internet situation remained dire, we worked harder to simplify complex concepts to make them accessible to everyone. Additionally, we made many articles and tutorial videos available so that everyone could perform complex configurations.

On the client side, existing apps were not as user-friendly as they should have been. Our parents, for example, couldn’t connect with them at all.

To address this, we first created custom versions of Hiddify Clash for Android and desktop to make the user connection process easier.

Gradually, your support for the project grew, and this provided extra motivation to add more features to the panel. We developed the multi-user version of the panel, redesigned many components, improved structures, and set up a support group on Telegram.

On the client side, after developing several versions of the Hiddify Clash app, many bugs in the Clash Meta core led us to seek an alternative solution.

After thoroughly reviewing and redesigning the entire client process based on performance tests, we decided to use the best market solutions. This led to the birth of the custom HiddifyNG and HiddifyN versions, which were warmly welcomed by you all.

For example, HiddifyNG was downloaded more than 100,000 times on Google Play and received a 4.8 out of 5 rating from you, which is incredible for an app less than five months old.

At the same time, on the server side, we added new protocols and introduced more features, including automatic CDN IP selection, simultaneous use of multiple domains, adding intermediate nodes, and many other features that cannot all be mentioned here.

docs.title: One-Year Anniversary of Hiddify
docs.text:
On our first anniversary:

On the client side, we introduced the cross-platform HiddifyNext app for Android, Windows, Linux, and Mac, and we will soon release it for iOS as well.

Our goal was to make it easy for developers to implement new protocols across all operating systems and to maintain integration across platforms.

The new app design is simple, performs efficiently, and uses minimal system resources. We will continue to add more exciting new features to it.

If you are a panel developer, you can read here how to integrate your panel with the app.

On the server side, in addition to previous protocols like Vless, Vmess, and Trojan, we introduced newer protocols such as Reality gRPC, WebSocket, H2, and SSH. In the panel’s beta version, protocols like Hysteria2 and TUICv5 with unified user management are now available and can easily be accessed in the beta version. They will be officially released soon.

If you would like to test the beta version and use the newer protocols, you can find out how to upgrade to the beta here. The next stable panel release will be the most bug-free and fastest version yet, so it will remain in beta for a longer period.

Everything that has been done so far has been spontaneous, voluntary, and without any financial gain. All the donations from you have gone toward the project and will continue to do so.

Through this difficult journey, we sincerely thank everyone who has helped us in any way to ensure that the dear people of our country remain connected to the free internet and can emerge from this absolute darkness.

We are also grateful to everyone who has fought for the internet for all.

To all of you who have continuously supported and stood by us on this journey, we are deeply thankful.

We hope for a day when no one is oppressed or controlled by authoritarian regimes.

docs.title: The Story of Hiddify: From Birth to Today
docs.text:
A detailed report to our dear supporters on the actions taken over the past two years

Greetings to all Hiddify supporters,

It was around this time two years ago when we all found ourselves in a great shock, and everyone tried to help in any way they could. This was the beginning of our journey.

The anniversary of the start of our activities is a reminder of deep sorrow, a great grief that united us in pursuit of a right we are all entitled to.

❤️ Freedom

Internet freedom, freedom of thought, political freedom, economic freedom, and freedom in all aspects of life.

We fought for internet freedom because we believed, and still do, that this freedom would lead to other freedoms as well.

In late September 2022, after people's access to free internet became even more restricted, we decided to do what we could by providing simple access to the internet, making things easier for the people of our beloved country. And so, Hiddify was born around this time.

At first, we tried to do a review of censorship methods and compile a list of VPS providers so that anyone with a bit of technical knowledge could buy a server and set up a VPN. We shared this list in the Awesome-Freedom repository.

Then, in October of the same year, we created a very easy and free installation guide for Microsoft Azure.

In November, we expanded the project to other datacenters, including quick setups in Hetzner, Oracle Cloud, Vultr, and OVH. The goal was to enable everyone to set up their own server without any technical knowledge.

docs.title: The Release of the First Version of HiddifyManager
docs.text:
In December 2022, we developed the first version of HiddifyManager and focused on teaching users how to activate it on the client side. We also made sure HiddifyManager was resistant to VPN detection bots, obtained valid certificates, set up security settings, and provided suitable configurations for users.

As time passed and the catastrophic internet situation continued, we pushed further to simplify complex concepts, making them accessible to everyone. Additionally, we made numerous articles and tutorial videos available to help people with the more complicated configurations.

On the other hand, existing client apps weren't simple enough for non-tech users—our parents couldn’t even figure them out.

To solve this, in January 2023, we developed custom versions of HiddifyClash for Android and desktop to make the connection process easier for users.

docs.title: Release of Version 1 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: As your support for the project grew, it gave us extra motivation to launch a support group on Telegram in February 2023. We also added more features to the panel, and in March 2023, after several initial releases, Version 1 of HiddifyManager was launched with the ability to create multiple users and domains, and many structural improvements.

docs.title: Release of Version 2 of HiddifyManager
docs.text:
Before Nowruz (the Persian New Year) in 2023, we released Version 2 of HiddifyManager, which introduced new features such as: - PWA web application support - Tutorial videos in the panel when clicking on ❓ - The ability to choose protocol ports, edit proxy names, and add fingerprints.

Around that time, we found out that Xray developers had included us on their list of approved web panels, which was a great feeling because they found us on their own.

During the same period, we added an automatic subdomain link creation feature based on the user's operator with the help of our friends at IRCF and introduced the AutoCDN domain.

docs.title: Release of Version 3 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: In April 2023, we redesigned the panel and released Version 3 of HiddifyManager, focusing on both stability and simplicity. In this version: - The dashboard was redesigned, adding tiles to monitor processes and resource usage, as well as the ability to see online users and their data usage. - All pages were redesigned, and a dark mode was added to the panel. - A search function was added to the settings, and other graphical improvements were made.

docs.title: Release of Version 4 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: In May 2023, we released Version 4 of HiddifyManager, which introduced support for the new Reality protocol. Other notable features in this version included: - Multi-admin support with separate access levels - Telegram bot integration with the panel - Custom domain support for sub-links - Automatic domain configuration in Cloudflare

docs.title: Release of Version 5 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: Due to your growing support and requests for additional protocols, we continued developing the panel and introduced Version 5 of HiddifyManager later that month, which included: - ShadowTLS v3 protocol support - Panel theme changes - User creation limits for admins and agents.

docs.title: Development of HiddifyN and HiddifyNG Apps
docs.text:
On the client side, after developing several versions of HiddifyClash, numerous bugs in the Clash Meta core led us to search for an alternative.

After reviewing and redesigning the entire client process with performance testing, we eventually launched custom versions of HiddifyNG and HiddifyN in April 2023, which were warmly received by you.

For example, HiddifyNG was downloaded over 100,000 times on Google Play in less than five months and received a 4.8/5 rating from you, which is an outstanding achievement for such a young app.

docs.title: Release of Version 6 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: On the server side, in May 2023, we added Fragment and Warp+ to HiddifyManager, releasing Version 6. Warp ensured that the server's IP remained hidden at the endpoint, while Fragment facilitated easier packet transmission through filtering. We also integrated the SingBox core, making HiddifyManager the only panel supporting two cores with accounting on the SingBox core.

docs.title: Release of Version 7 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: In June 2023, we released Version 7 of HiddifyManager, which introduced several important protocols and features, including: - Support for multiple Reality domains and workers - Redesigned domain addition page - Warp version 2

docs.title: Release of Version 7 of HiddifyN and HiddifyNG Apps
docs.text: In line with continued client software development, we introduced routing and load-balancing features in HiddifyNG and HiddifyN.

docs.title: Release of Version 8 of HiddifyManager
docs.text: Later, in addition to previous protocols like Vless, Vmess, Trojan, Reality, gRPC, WebSocket, and H2, with the help of a friend, we added the secure SSH protocol to Version 8 of HiddifyManager in July 2023. This version also introduced important new features, such as: - Temporary short links, inspired by Inspector Gadget - Smart sub-link creation - Simplified VPN activation for users.

docs.title: Start of HiddifyApp Multi-Platform Development
docs.text:
On the client side, we started developing the cross-platform HiddifyApp for Android, Windows, Linux, and Mac in October 2023, in honor of our first anniversary.

Our goal was to make it easy for developers to implement new protocols across all platforms and ensure consistency between systems.

The new app was designed to be very simple, highly efficient, and lightweight.

docs.title: Release of the Hiddify Reality Scanner
docs.text: In November 2023, as restrictions on the Reality protocol intensified, we released a Reality Scanner. This tool helps users identify appropriate SNI domains for Reality, assisting them in bypassing the new limitations. This marked an important step in ensuring continuous, reliable access to internet freedom in the face of evolving censorship techniques.

docs.title: Celebrating Two Years of Hiddify
docs.text: Now, as we celebrate Hiddify’s second anniversary, we reflect on all we have accomplished together. From the humble beginnings of open-source guides and community-driven efforts to the development of a powerful suite of tools for both users and administrators, Hiddify has become a trusted name for internet freedom.

docs.title: What’s Next?
docs.text:
Looking ahead, we are committed to staying on the cutting edge of censorship circumvention. The next year will see us expanding Hiddify’s features, improving performance, and enhancing security to keep pace with new challenges.

We plan to: - Improve user experience across all platforms, ensuring that even less tech-savvy individuals can benefit from Hiddify’s capabilities. - Continue building community resources and fostering collaboration with other freedom-focused organizations. - Launch more educational tools and resources to empower users to deploy and manage their own instances of Hiddify.

Together, we will continue the fight for internet freedom.

docs.title: Thank You to Our Community
docs.text:
None of this would have been possible without the support of our incredible community. We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your continuous feedback, encouragement, and contributions to the Hiddify project.

Let’s keep pushing forward, fighting for a freer and more open internet.

With gratitude, The Hiddify Team ❤️

docs.title: 🎉 HiddifyManager Version 11 Released!
docs.text:
Packed with exciting improvements and updates. Here’s a summary of the key changes:

  • 🔹 XHTTP protocol added

  • 🔹 Support for separate domains for upload and download Now you can separate upload and download traffic using different domains or ALPNs, helping reduce the chance of detection.

  • 🔹 Complete redesign of the proxy system You can now fully customize the parameters of each proxy to your preferences. ✨

  • 🔹 Xray core upgraded to version 25.6 Brings improved performance, enhanced security, and new backend features.

  • 🔹 QUIC protocol support added In addition to H1, H2, WS, and HTTPUpgrade, QUIC is now supported with CDN compatibility.

  • 🔹 Updated HAProxy version (Ubuntu 24.04 only) Provides more accurate and faster proxy routing.

  • 🔹 Admin panel password protection added An extra layer of security for admin access.

  • 🔹 Reduced RAM and CPU usage RAM consumption reduced by up to 50%, with optimized resource management. 💪

You can now delete, activate, deactivate, or reset day and traffic for selected users — all at once! 🚀

docs.title: Hiddify Core
docs.text:
Hiddify Core (hiddify-core, the HiddifyCli binary) is the proxy core that runs inside the Hiddify app on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux. You can also run it on its own, from the command line, on a server, a router (OpenWrt) or a desktop without a screen.

It is built on hiddify-sing-box, Hiddify's fork of sing-box. Every sing-box config works in it, and it adds many protocols, transports and anti-censorship features that upstream sing-box does not have. Around this core, hiddify-core adds a config builder: give it a share link, a subscription or a config in almost any format, and it builds a complete client config for you, with a local proxy or a TUN, DNS, routing and proxy groups.

Hiddify Core at a glance

  • Download: hiddify-core releases on GitHub, for Linux, Windows and macOS, many processors, and OpenWrt packages.
  • Source code: hiddify-core and hiddify-sing-box.
  • Command-line reference: every command and flag.
  • Features of the core: Hiddify sing-box features, with a page for each protocol, transport and DNS feature.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
On Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, OpenWrt and others), this command finds your system and processor, installs /usr/bin/hiddify-core and sets up a service (systemd, or procd on OpenWrt):

bash <(curl https://i.hiddify.com/core)

The service runs hiddify-core -D /var/lib/hiddify-core run -c /etc/hiddify-core/config.json. Edit /etc/hiddify-core/config.json, then restart it with systemctl restart hiddify-core (/etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart on OpenWrt).

Other ways:

  • Download by hand: take the archive for your system from the releases page and unpack it. On Linux, keep the lib folder next to HiddifyCli. On Windows, run HiddifyCli.exe from a terminal.
  • Docker: docker pull ghcr.io/hiddify/hiddify-core:latest, or docker-compose up -d in the docker folder of the repository.

In the examples on this site the binary is called HiddifyCli; after the Linux installer it is hiddify-core. Both are the same program.

docs.title: Run a config: run or srun
docs.text:
hiddify-core has two ways to run a config. Pick the one that matches what you have.

You have Use What happens Share links (vless://, hy2://, wg://…), a subscription link, a Clash or Xray config, or only the outbounds of a sing-box config run hiddify-core reads the proxies, builds the rest of the config (local proxy or TUN, DNS, routing, groups) from the Hiddify settings, and runs it A complete sing-box config that must run exactly as written (inbounds, DNS, route and all) srun hiddify-core runs the config as it is, like sing-box run, with every Hiddify feature available

docs.title: run: from proxies to a ready client
docs.text:
# a file of share links, one per line, or a base64 subscription
HiddifyCli run -c links.txt

# a subscription URL; it is updated again when the server sends profile-update-interval
HiddifyCli run -c https://example.com/sub/abc

# only the outbounds of a sing-box config are used
HiddifyCli run -c outbounds.json

By default run opens a mixed (HTTP and SOCKS5) proxy on 127.0.0.1:12334, groups the proxies under a selector with automatic tests, and sends DNS to 1.1.1.1. Point your browser or system at that proxy, or let hiddify-core do it:

# a system-wide VPN (needs root or administrator)
sudo HiddifyCli run -c links.txt --tun

# set the system proxy of the desktop
HiddifyCli run -c links.txt --system-proxy

# your Hiddify app settings (Settings → ⋮ → Export → "Export all options to file")
HiddifyCli run -c links.txt -d hiddify-settings.json

run accepts all of these as input:

  • share links of every protocol the app supports, one per line, plain or base64;
  • subscription links, also inside a file next to other links;
  • a sing-box JSON config: a whole config (only its outbounds and endpoints are taken), a list of outbounds, or a single outbound;
  • a Clash or mihomo YAML config (its proxies);
  • an Xray JSON config;
  • a WireGuard .conf file.

With --full-config, run also keeps the inbounds, DNS and route rules of a sing-box input and builds its own parts next to them. When the config must run without any change, use srun.

docs.title: srun: a full sing-box config as it is
docs.text:
HiddifyCli srun -c config.json

srun is the run command of sing-box. It takes a complete config, with your own inbounds, DNS, route and experimental sections, and adds nothing to it. All sing-box options work, together with the Hiddify additions: XHTTP, finalmask, WARP, AmneziaWG, DNS tunnels, the balancer and the rest (see Hiddify sing-box features).

# several files are merged, in the order of their names
HiddifyCli srun -c base.json -c outbounds.json

# every .json file of a folder
HiddifyCli srun -C /etc/hiddify-core/conf.d

# read the config from standard input
cat config.json | HiddifyCli srun -c stdin

Send SIGHUP to reload the config without stopping (the new config is checked first); SIGINT or SIGTERM stop it. srun is also the way to run a server with hiddify-core, since a server config is mostly inbounds.

Turn proxies into a full config, then edit it

HiddifyCli parse links.txt -o outbounds.json converts links to sing-box outbounds, and HiddifyCli build -c outbounds.json -o config.json builds the full client config that run would use. Edit config.json and run it with srun. See the CLI reference.

docs.title: How it differs from sing-box, Xray and mihomo
docs.text: hiddify-core sing-box Xray-core mihomo Based on a fork of sing-box 1.15, with Hiddify's additions — its own core, from the V2Ray family a fork of Clash Config format sing-box JSON sing-box JSON Xray JSON Clash YAML Inputs it reads share links, subscriptions, sing-box JSON, Xray JSON, Clash and mihomo YAML, WireGuard .conf sing-box JSON Xray JSON Clash YAML, and link subscriptions in proxy providers Builds a client config from bare proxies yes, with run (TUN or proxy, DNS, rules, groups) no, you write the whole config no, you write the whole config no, you write the whole config Control API gRPC (used by the Hiddify app) and the Clash API Clash API gRPC REST (Clash API)

docs.title: Compared with sing-box
docs.text:
hiddify-core runs every sing-box config, and adds:

  • Xray's transports in sing-box: XHTTP, mKCP, XDRIVE, finalmask, the raw transport, VLESS encryption and multi-segment gRPC paths, so configs made for Xray load as they are.
