docs.title: How to transfer files between a server and a computer
How to transfer files between a server and a computer
docs.text:
This page shows you how to copy files from your server to your computer and back, for example to keep a copy of a Hiddify backup or to upload a file to the server.

Only need a panel backup?

You do not need any commands for that. In the Hiddify admin panel, open the Backup & restore page and click Download backup. See How to back up and restore the panel.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You know your server's IP address and SSH username (usually root), and you can connect to it over SSH.
  • Open a terminal on your computer:
    • Windows: PowerShell
    • macOS: Terminal
    • Linux: Terminal

This page uses scp, a command that copies files over SSH. It is already included in Windows 10 and 11, macOS and Linux.

If Windows says scp is not recognized

Open PowerShell as administrator (right-click PowerShell, then Run as administrator) and run this command to install the OpenSSH client:

Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0

Then close PowerShell and open it again.

docs.title: Find the file on the server
docs.text:
Hiddify Manager saves an automatic backup of the panel every 6 hours in /opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/. To see the list, connect to the server over SSH and run:

ls /opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/

You will see files named by date and time, like 2026_10_20__06_00_03.json:

Pick the file you want to copy and note its name.

docs.title: Copy a file from the server to your computer
docs.text:
Run this on your own computer, not on the server. The general form is:

scp <user>@<server-ip>:<path/on/server> "<folder on your computer>"

Example: your username is root, the server IP is 1.1.1.1, and you want to copy a backup into the folder C:\Backup:

scp root@1.1.1.1:/opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/2026_10_20__06_00_03.json "C:\Backup"

Type your server password (or key passphrase) when asked. It worked if the file now appears in C:\Backup.

docs.title: Copy a file from your computer to the server
docs.text:
Run this on your own computer. Example: the file C:\File\text.txt should go to the /root/ folder on the server:

scp "C:\File\text.txt" root@1.1.1.1:/root/

To check, connect to the server over SSH and run:

ls /root/

It worked if text.txt is in the list.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
• No such file or directory: the path is wrong. Check it with ls on the server, and remember that Linux paths are case-sensitive (hiddify-manager, not Hiddify-Manager).
  • Permission denied: the username, password or key is wrong, or the user cannot read or write that folder. Use root or a folder your user owns.
  • Connection timed out: the server IP or SSH port is wrong. If you changed the SSH port, add -P with the port number (capital P for scp), for example scp -P 2222 ....

docs.title: Use the web panel instead
docs.text: In Hiddify Manager v14, the admin panel has an SSH terminal page with a built-in file browser. You can upload files to the server and download files from it there, without a separate program. Avoid entering your server password on third-party websites.

docs.title: TLS setting for increased security
docs.text:
This page shows you how to make TLS connections that go through a CDN harder to detect. You need it if you use a Cloudflare CDN domain with Hiddify and your connections are unstable on some Internet providers.

TLS is the encryption that protects https connections. Filtering systems can study patterns in TLS traffic, and older TLS versions show more of these patterns. TLS 1.3, the newest version, encrypts more of the connection setup and is harder to recognise.

docs.title: Set the minimum TLS version on Cloudflare
docs.text:
Symptom: your CDN (Cloudflare) configs connect on some operators but are unstable or don't connect on others.

Likely cause: Cloudflare still accepts older TLS versions for your domain.

Fix: tell Cloudflare to accept only TLS 1.3.

  1. Log in to your Cloudflare account and select your domain.
  2. In the menu, open SSL/TLS, then Edge Certificates.
  3. Find Minimum TLS Version and set it to TLS 1.3.

What to check: reconnect from a device on the operator that had problems.

If it still doesn't work: try a new subdomain. The filtering system may have already detected the old subdomain.

docs.title: TLS 1.3 on your device
docs.text:
The Hiddify app and other Xray or sing-box based apps have their own built-in TLS. They don't use your operating system's TLS settings, so you normally don't need to change anything on your phone or computer.

Windows 11, macOS and most recent Linux versions already have TLS 1.3 turned on for their own programs.

Optional: turn on TLS 1.2 and 1.3 in Windows 10 settings

This only affects programs that use Windows' built-in TLS. Microsoft does not officially support TLS 1.3 in Windows 10, so this may have no effect. Change the Windows registry only if you know what you are doing.

  1. Open Notepad and paste the text below:

    Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Client]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Server]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.3\Client]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.3\Server]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001

  2. Save the file with a .reg extension, for example tls.reg. In the Save as type list, choose All files so the file doesn't end in .txt.

  3. Double-click the file and confirm the prompts.
  4. Restart your computer.
  5. To check: press Win+R, type regedit and press Enter. Go to the path shown in the picture below. The TLS versions you turned on are listed there.

Warning

Older versions of this page also turned on SSL 3.0. SSL 3.0 is old and insecure. If you used that file, delete the SSL 3.0 key under the same registry path.

docs.title: Troubleshooting connectivity issues with HiddifyManager and proxies
docs.text:
Why don't my connections connect even though HiddifyManager is installed?

Or, what is the story behind this that it connects with One ISP but does not connect with other one, for example?

Follow this article to the end to answer these questions.

As mentioned in the preliminaries of HiddifyManager configuration installation, there are several reasons for this issue:

  1. IP or domain is blocked.
  2. The IP is semi-blocked and placed in the yellow list. For example, it is connected in some ISPs and not in others.
  3. If a CDN domain is used, the Cloudflare IP is not selected.

Therefore, this panel is not going to work miracles. It requires preliminary installation. Before configuring the panel, make sure your IP or domain is clean. How to test

If a CDN domain is used, you need to find Cloudflare Clean IP and in the mandatory field Enter the domain in the domains menu.

If you have been able to connect from another device, on the same server and the same domain, immediately send us the link of the Trojan or Wi-Las or Wi-Mes so that we can add it to the panel.

docs.title: Ways to solve the problem
docs.text:
• Find a clean IP
  • Use a new domain
  • You can use CDN
  • You can use Relay
  • Use the Fake domain

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyClashAndroid app
docs.text: This software is developed based on Clash and many features are included in it.

docs.title: Download the app
docs.text:
To do this, enter the Android tab in your user panel and open the section related to Hidify Android.

  • Click on Direct Download to download the application.

docs.title: Install the app
docs.text: Run the downloaded file to install the program. It may give an error that the source of the file is unknown, which you can confirm to install the file.

docs.title: Add profile to the app
docs.text:
• Here you need to get acquainted with a concept called profile. The profile is a yml file includes all the connections that can be accessed in this section. There are two types of profiles

  • Green or lite profile for filtered sites, in which case only filtered sites are passed through the VPN and other sites, including domestic sites, are opened without the VPN, which is a better mode. So you don't need to turn off VPN to open these sites.

  • The second mode is the orange or Normal profile, which passes all traffic through the VPN to the server. If domestic sites are blocked on the server, they will not be opened, or if WARP is enabled for all traffic, domestic sites will be opened via WARP.

  • Finally, choose one of the two profiles and click on Install so that the profile is automatically added to the program.

docs.title: Add profile manually
docs.text:
• Tap on Profile in the HiddifyClash app on Android.
  • And on the screen that opens, tap the + button.
  • On this page, go to the URL section.
  • And copy the selected profile link from the user page and place it here and save it.
  • The desired profile is added to the app.

docs.title: Connect to the app
docs.text: Click on the specified button to connect.

docs.title: Update profile
docs.text: To update the profile and configs, click on the profile. Then, on the opened page, click on the update sign so that the profile is updated according to the latest server changes.

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyNG app
docs.text:
This app is the best software for connecting to Xray protocols on Android operating system. Download and install the software

Enter the Android tab in your user panel and open the HiddifyNG section.

Click on Direct Download to download the application.

You can also download and install the program directly from GitHub and Google Play.

docs.title: Add config
docs.text: To do this, in the same section related to the HiddifyNG program, click on Click to Import to add the configuration to the program.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: This plate is designed for quick connection to the filter breaker, which consists of several parts.

docs.title: Profile section
docs.text:
In this section, you can see your imported profiles.

  • View the Traffic usage and the total traffic. Also see the number of days remaining in your account. (section number 1)

  • You can enter your user page in the panel through button number 2

  • You can contact your support through button number 3.

docs.title: Add new profile
docs.text:
For this, press the + button from the profile section or from the top right of the application.

You can use the copied link or scan its QR code.

docs.title: Connect to the software
docs.text: To do this, click on the connection button in the middle of the screen.

docs.title: Configs
docs.text: Here are the configs that were added using the subscription link.

docs.title: Update configs
docs.text: For this, use the update button number 2.

docs.title: Start or stop configs
docs.text: For this, use the update button number 3.

docs.title: Three-dot menu in configs
docs.text: In this menu, which is a subset of the config menu, you can do various things that are mentioned below.

docs.title: Filter configuration file
docs.text: This menu is for filtering configurations based on a specific item.

docs.title: Export non-custom configs
docs.text: This menu is used to exit the configuration added to the program and transfer it to another device.

docs.title: Remove all config
docs.text: This menu is for deleting the entire config file from the program.

docs.title: Remove duplicate config
docs.text: Sometimes, due to the large number of configurations, you need to sort and remove the duplicate imported configurations from the program. Use this option for this.

docs.title: Remove invalid config (Test first)
docs.text: Sometimes you manipulate the configs to get better results by changing the parameters. If you need to delete configs that have invalid settings, use this option.

docs.title: Real delay all configuration
docs.text: This option displays the result for actual ping test based on the connection to the configs.

docs.title: Sorting by test results
docs.text:
Sorts the list of configs based on the test result. Configurations with lower ping and better results are placed at the top of the list.

To do this, tap on the section related to the profile to open the section related to their settings.

You can edit the imported profiles or add a new profile.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: On this page, there are advanced settings that will be mentioned later.

docs.title: Proxy mode settings
docs.text: The settings of this section determine how the traffic of sites and applications pass through the VPN, which consists of three parts.

docs.title: All
docs.text: All sites and apps pass through the app.

docs.title: Blocked
docs.text: Passes detected filtered sites through the app.

docs.title: Not Opened
docs.text: In addition to the identified filter sites, it also passes through the app the sites whose filtering status is unknown.

docs.title: Fragment
docs.text:
Fragment splits the sent packets into some pieces. In this way, SNI is hidden from the GFW and filtering will be bypassed. more information

The settings in this section determine how information is transmitted in the form of fragmented packets. The purpose of applying these settings is to create resistance against the filtering system.

docs.title: Default
docs.text: Applies the fragment defined in the config or proxy link.

docs.title: Random
docs.text: It splits packets into random chunks.

docs.title: SNI
docs.text: It splits packets into two pieces.

docs.title: Connection mode
docs.text: The settings in this section determine how to connect to configs.

docs.title: Smart
docs.text: It will automatically connect to the configuration with the highest speed (lowest ping).

docs.title: Load Balance
docs.text: It connects to several configs at the same time and traffic is distributed between them. This mode is very useful when the IP related to the configs is not clean. By using this mode and spreading the load on several configs, an acceptable speed would be obtained.

docs.title: Manual
docs.text: Configs are entered manually. By clicking this button, the app opens another page that shows the list of available configs in which you can choose your desired one.

docs.title: Three-line software menu settings
docs.text: In this section, there are several general settings, the most useful parts of which are these.

docs.title: Subscription group setting
docs.text: Settings for all subscription links Select this option.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: There are general software settings in this section.

docs.title: Logcat
docs.text: Use this option if you need a log file for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Use this menu if you need to report bugs and errors.

docs.title: Tutorial for Nekobox app
docs.text: This application is one of the applications that can be used for Android, which works relatively well for old devices.

docs.title: Download the application
docs.text: To download, you can refer to the GitHub of the project here.

docs.title: Initial settings
docs.text:
• Activate the use system dns as direct dns option through Settings.
  • Also set subscription min tls version to 1.3.

Note: if you are using old devices, set tls to 1.2.

docs.title: Add subscription link
docs.text:
• Copy the subscription link of the user from the panel.
  • Enter the group section and create a new group.
  • Set the group type option to subscription.
  • Click on subscription link and enter the subscription link.
  • Enable force resolve and auto update options.

docs.title: Tutorial on making Proxy Chain
docs.text:
In this method, the traffic is transferred from one proxy to another, and it allows you to remain hidden or anonymous much longer than the previous methods, and also to be more secure.

  • Configure the add or import option through manual settings.

  • Select Proxy chain.

  • Click Add profile and select and enter, for example, a reality config.

  • For the second proxy, for example, we use Cloudflare worker and save the profile.

  • Now go here to check if it was done correctly. If Cloudflare's IP is seen, it means the job is done correctly.

Note: When using this method, the ping test may encounter an error, which is a bug that needs to be fixed. But the filter connection is established and there is no problem.

You can also use http and socks5 in this method.

You can also use more than 2 proxies to connect at the same time.

docs.title: Install the app

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyClashDesktop software
docs.text: This software is developed based on Clash and many features are included in it.

docs.title: Downloading the software
docs.text:
For this, enter the Desktop tab in your user panel and open the section related to HiddifyClash.

You can download the software based on your operating system from the section number 3 indicated in the image above.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Installing the program is very simple and is completed with a few next steps.

docs.title: Mac
docs.text: For Mac, you must confirm the program in the privacy section.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text: For Linux, you only need to give executable access to the downloaded AppImage file and run it.

docs.title: Adding a profile to the app
docs.text:
For this, enter the Desktop tab in your user panel and open the section related to HiddifyClash.

  • Here you need to get acquainted with a concept called profile. The profile of a yml file includes all the connections that can be accessed in this section. There are two types of profiles

  • Green or lite profile for filtered sites, in which case only filtered sites are passed through the filter breaker and other sites, including Iranian sites, are opened without the filter breaker, which is a better mode. So you don't need to turn off VPN to open these sites.

  • The second mode is the orange or normal profile, which sends all traffic from the filter breaker to the server. If Iranian sites are blocked on the server, they will not be opened, or if warp is enabled for all traffic, Iranian sites will be opened with warp.

  • Finally, choose one of the two profiles from section number 4.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Click on install profile, the profile will be automatically added to the program. You can also import the copied link in the profile section manually in section 1.

In section number 2, the information related to the imported profile, including the expiration date and the total traffic volume and the traffic volume consumed, can be seen.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: In this menu, you can turn the filter breaker on or off with the Enable anti-censorship button.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text: In this menu, you can specify how to run proxies (configs), which includes 3 main sections.

docs.title: Rule
docs.text: This mode executes proxies based on the rules in the imported profile, which contains several sections.

docs.title: PROXY
docs.text: This subsection executes the proxies in the profile and connects to the first config that pings.

docs.title: automatic
docs.text: In this case, it connects to the best configuration that has a lower ping.

docs.title: sequential
docs.text: In this case, the proxies are connected in turn, that is, the load is divided in a way, but the main difference with Load-balance is that in Load-balance, it is connected to several configurations at the same time, but in this case, it is connected to one configuration at the moment.

docs.title: Sort by location
docs.text: By using button number 1, you can sort the configurations based on location.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: You can test connections by using button number 2.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: This mode is for manual configuration selection and is useful when you want to use a specific configuration.

docs.title: Sort by location
docs.text: By using button number 1, you can sort the configurations based on location.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: You can test connections by using button number 2.

docs.title: Direct
docs.text: This mode sends the traffic directly to the Internet and the traffic does not pass through the filter breaker.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
In this menu, the general settings of the software are made.

  • Button number 1 or TUN Mode is for tunneling the entire system traffic.

Note: To activate this button, the software must be run with admin access in Windows, i.e. Run as Administrator. It should also be run on Mac and Linux with admin or root access.

  • Button number 2 activates the proxy system and is used for software that has proxy capabilities. That is, after activating this button, you should be able to connect to the filter breaker in the proxy section of the software on IP 127.0.0.1 and the default port of the program is 7890.

This mode is useful when you don't want to pass all your traffic through the VPN.

  • Button number 3 or Auto Launch runs the software automatically after the system boots up.

  • Button number 4 or Silent Start makes the software run inconspicuously and its icon is displayed in the task bar.

  • You can turn off IP version 6 using button number 5.

  • In section 6, you can determine the software port, the default of which is 7890.

  • In section 7, you can determine the core of the software, the default of which is Clash Meta.

  • In section number 8, you can determine the language.

  • In section number 9, you can change the theme related to the software.

  • The software version can be seen in section 10.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: In this section, the connections established in the software are displayed. That is, if a program uses a filter, it will be displayed in this section, which is very useful for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: This menu is related to the rules in the imported profile, which can be seen in this file.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: In this section, the log related to the software can be seen, which is very useful during troubleshooting.

docs.title: Traffic graph
docs.text: In the specified section below, the graphic related to the traffic passing through the filter breaker is also displayed.

docs.title: Proxy modes
docs.text: One of the most important parts of this application is the proxy modes, which will be explained about each part below.

docs.title: Auto/Smart
docs.text: It will automatically connect to the configuration with the highest speed (lowest ping).

docs.title: Load-Balance
docs.text: It connects to several configs at the same time and traffic is distributed between them. This mode is very useful when you have several configurations with dirty IP, by spreading the load on several configurations at the same time, an acceptable speed is obtained.

docs.title: Connection to the VPN

docs.title: Advanced settings
docs.text:
This section is opened by pressing the Manual button in the proxy mode section.

The advanced settings of the program are located in this section. In this subsection, there are optional settings of the program, which includes several different sections. * `Core: basic settings` that do not need to be changed for everyday use. The only widely used option is the port used for the program, which can be changed in this section. If you need to use proxy, you can set socks5 proxy on this port. *V2rayN Settings This section contains the default settings of the V2rayN program, which is the main basis of the HIddifyN program. > * which Start on boot runs the program when the system boots. > * Auto hide startup automatically hides the program running at the beginning of the work, and only the program icon is visible in the Notification Area. > * Check for pre release update gives unofficial updates to the program. > * Also, in the settings you see in the picture below, which of course are not used for everyday use. * System proxy settings This section shows the settings related to the proxy system. * Tun mode settings This section contains Tun mode settings that do not need to be changed for everyday use. * Core type settings In this section, you can set kernels for different protocols, the default of which is Xray. ###### Routing setting In this section, you can view the routing related to the profile imported to the program and make changes to it if needed. But it is suggested not to touch it if possible. ###### DNS setting In this section, you can enter your desired DNS into the software. ###### Reboot as administrator With this option, you can restart the program and open it with admin access, which is required to use Tun mode.

docs.title: Tutorial for Fair VPN app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your Hiddify subscription to the free Fair VPN app on iPhone and iPad, test the connections, and share your VPN with other devices.

Recommended: Hiddify App

The easiest app for a Hiddify server is the free Hiddify App. It is on the App Store. See How to install Hiddify App.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Fair VPN from the App Store. It is free.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal Hiddify page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). A config is the settings for one connection to the server.

docs.title: Get your subscription link
docs.text:
Fair VPN is not in the app list on the Hiddify user page, so you add the link by hand.

  1. Open your user page link.
  2. Open the menu and tap All Configs.
  3. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link b64 and tap Get Link. A small window opens with a QR code and a Copy Link button.

Note

The screenshots of the user page come from an older panel version. The current page looks different, but the link is the same.

Now you can either copy the link or scan its QR code.

docs.title: Option 1: Copy the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

    1. Open Fair VPN. In the VPN tab, tap Import VPN Configs.

    2. Paste the link and tap OK.

    After a few seconds, your configs appear in the app.

docs.title: Option 2: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
Use this if the user page is open on another screen, such as a computer.

  1. In Fair VPN, open the VPN tab and tap Add VPN by QR Code in the bottom menu.

  2. Point your phone's camera at the QR code on the user page. The configs are added, just as with option 1.

docs.title: Test the connections
docs.text:
1. Tap Test VPN Latency.
  2. Tap Test Web Latency.

The app makes a real test through each config and shows the result next to it. Latency is how long a reply takes; lower is better.

docs.title: Sort configs by test result
docs.text:
1. Tap Test VPN Latency.
  2. Tap Sort by Latency.

The configs are now sorted by their test result, best first.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text:
Fair VPN cannot refresh a subscription by itself. To get the latest configs:

  1. Tap Delete All VPN to remove all configs.
  2. Add the subscription link again, as shown above.

If your admin uses Auto CDN

To get a new clean IP, delete all configs with Delete All VPN. Then turn the VPN off, reload your user page, and add the subscription link again.

docs.title: Share your VPN with other devices
docs.text:
You can share your phone's VPN with another device on the same Wi-Fi network, for example a device that can't install a VPN app.

  1. In Fair VPN, turn on Local Sharing. The app shows an IP address and a port.

  2. On the other device, open its network proxy settings.

  3. Enter the IP address and port shown by Fair VPN, and save.

The other device now uses your phone's VPN connection.

docs.title: Tutorial for FoXray app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your Hiddify subscription to the FoXray app on iPhone and iPad and how to use its main settings. FoXray comes from the team behind the WingsX app, and replaced WingsX after WingsX was removed from the App Store.

FoXray is no longer on the App Store

As of October 2026, FoXray's App Store page (id6448898396) no longer exists, so you can't install it any more. If you already have it, the steps below still describe how it works. For a new install, use the Hiddify App (App Store, see How to install Hiddify App) or another app from the iOS client list.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• FoXray already installed on your iPhone or iPad.
  • Your user page link. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal Hiddify page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). FoXray can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Add your subscription link
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link.
  2. Open the menu and tap All Configs.
  3. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link b64 and tap Get Link.

  4. Tap Copy Link.

    The screenshot shows an older version of the user page, which had an **iOS** tab. The current page looks different.
    1. Open FoXray and tap Subscriptions in the bottom menu.

    2. Tap the + button.

    3. Type any name you like.

    4. Paste the link into the URL field.

    5. Tap Subscribe. Your configs are added to the app.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text: In the Subscriptions menu, tap the ↪️ icon. Your links are updated.

docs.title: Add a subscription with a QR code
docs.text:
1. In the FoXray menu, tap the QR code button.
  2. Point the camera at the QR code of the link or config. It is added to the app.

If the QR code is saved as a photo on your phone:

  1. In the FoXray menu, tap the photo button.
  2. Choose the photo. The configs are added.

docs.title: Add a single config
docs.text:
We don't recommend this, because a single config can't be updated. Use it only if you need to.

  1. On your user page, open All Configs and copy one config from Individual Configs.
  2. In FoXray, tap the Clipboard icon in the FoXray menu. The copied config is added.

docs.title: Test the connections
docs.text:
First choose the test type:

  1. Go to Setting, then the Speed Test section.
  2. Under PingType, choose TCPPing, TLSPing or RealPing. RealPing gives the most realistic result.

Then, on the main page of the app, tap the connection test icon.

docs.title: Limit memory use
docs.text: Go to Setting, then ToolBox, and turn on Limit Memory Usage.

docs.title: Add a DNS server
docs.text:
A DNS server turns website names into IP addresses.

  1. In the FoXray menu, open the DNS section.
  2. Tap +.
  3. Type any name.
  4. Enter the DNS address you want in the Default DNS Address field.
  5. Leave the other fields as they are and save.

docs.title: Premium features
docs.text: The following features are only available if you bought the premium version of the app.

docs.title: Update subscriptions automatically
docs.text: Go to Setting and turn on Auto Update Subscription.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: Go to Setting, then Pro ToolBox, and turn on Always On. Your VPN then stays on all the time.

docs.title: Show the server location
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Show Location. After you connect, the app shows where the server is.

docs.title: Pin the connected config
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Pin Outbound. The connected config is pinned to the top of the main page.

docs.title: Test configs before connecting
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Test Outbound before Start. The app tests the configs before it connects.

docs.title: Turn on fragment
docs.text:
Fragment splits the first TLS packet into small pieces, which can help get past filtering. Read more in How the TLS trick works.

  1. Tap the connection in the app.
  2. Turn on Fragment.

  3. Enter these suggested values:

    packets: tlshello
length: 100-200
interval: 10-20

Depending on your internet provider, you may need other values. You can also change the packet type from tlshello to TCP segments 1-3, although filtering may detect this mode sooner:

packets: 1-3

docs.title: Tutorial for ShadowRocket app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your Hiddify subscription to Shadowrocket on iPhone and iPad, and how to use its most useful settings. Shadowrocket is a paid app that works with Xray-based configs.

Recommended: Hiddify App

The easiest app for a Hiddify server is the free Hiddify App. It is on the App Store. See How to install Hiddify App.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Buy and install Shadowrocket from the App Store.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal Hiddify page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). Shadowrocket can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.
  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap Shadowrocket. If you don't see it, tap View More. You can also download the app from here.
  4. Tap Import To App. Shadowrocket opens and adds your subscription.

If that doesn't work, add the link by hand as shown below.

Lite and Normal configs no longer exist

Older versions of the user page offered two kinds of configs in an iOS tab: Lite (only blocked sites go through the VPN) and Normal (all traffic goes through the VPN). The current user page has no iOS tab and no Lite/Normal choice. If you want local sites to open without the VPN, ask your admin; this is set on the server. If your admin turned on WARP, local sites can open through WARP.

docs.title: Add your subscription by hand
docs.text:
First get the link:

  1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link and tap Get Link. A window with a QR code and a Copy Link button opens.

Then add it to Shadowrocket in one of two ways.

docs.title: Copy and paste the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

  2. Open Shadowrocket and tap the + button in the top-right corner.

    1. Set Type to Subscribe.
    2. Paste the link into the URL field.

    3. Tap Save.

    All your configs now load in the app.

docs.title: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
1. On the Shadowrocket home screen, tap the scanner button.

  2. Scan the QR code shown on your user page. Your configs are added to the app.

docs.title: Test the configs
docs.text:
On the home screen, tap Connectivity Test. The app tests each config.

For more realistic results:

  1. Tap Settings in the bottom menu.
  2. Set Test Method to Connect.
  3. Run the test again.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text: Tap the update icon above the configs of a subscription. The configs are updated with the latest settings from the server.

docs.title: Subscription settings
docs.text: Go to Settings and tap Subscribe near the bottom. Here you can set:

docs.title: Update when the app opens
docs.text: Turn on Update on Open.

docs.title: Update automatically in the background
docs.text: Turn on Auto Background Update. The app then refreshes your subscriptions at regular intervals.

docs.title: Sort by ping
docs.text: Turn on Sort by ping to list the configs by their test result, best first.

docs.title: Prevent IP leaks
docs.text:
An IP leak means a website can see your real IP address even though the VPN is on.

  1. Go to Settings, then UDP.
  2. Turn on Disable STUN.

docs.title: Fix missing sound in some apps
docs.text:
If some apps (for example Clubhouse) play no sound:

  1. Go to Settings, then TCP.
  2. Change the Fingerprint value.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Go to Settings, then Shortcuts. Here you can set a voice command for an action, for example to start the VPN.

docs.title: Keep the VPN on (On Demand)
docs.text: Go to Settings, then On Demand.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: When this is on, your VPN always stays on.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: When this is on and your connection drops, Shadowrocket blocks all internet traffic so your real IP address is not exposed.

docs.title: Disconnect on Sleep
docs.text: When this is on, the VPN disconnects when the phone goes to sleep.

docs.title: Share your VPN with other devices
docs.text:
You can share your VPN with another device on the same network, for example a device that can't install a VPN app.

  1. Go to Settings, then Proxy.
  2. Tap Proxy Share.

  3. Turn on Enable Share. The app shows an IP address and a port.

  4. On the other device, open its network proxy settings and enter that IP address and port.

The other device now uses your VPN without installing anything.

docs.title: Create a load balancer
docs.text:
A load balancer spreads your traffic over several configs, so one slow or blocked config doesn't stop you.

  1. On the home screen, hold your finger on the screen and swipe down. A hidden menu opens.

  2. Tap the + button.

  3. Type any name.

  4. Set Type to load-balance.
  5. Under Policy, select the configs to use: the ones with the best ping, or all of them.
  6. Leave Interval (time between tests) and Timeout (how long a config may fail and still count as working) at their default values, unless you know what you need.

  7. Tap Save.

  8. Tap the new load balancer, then tap Test. This tests it and connects through it.

When you turn Shadowrocket on or off, the load balancer turns on or off with it.

docs.title: Fix sites or apps that don't open
docs.text:
If some sites or apps don't open, or Telegram GIFs don't load:

  1. Go to Settings.
  2. Open TCP.
  3. Set TLS to Network.
  4. Set Fingerprint to Safari15_5.
  5. Set Max Read Length to 16384.
  6. Go back to Home.
  7. Set Global Routing to Proxy.

docs.title: Tutorial for SingBox app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your Hiddify subscription to the official sing-box app on iPhone and iPad, and how to connect. It is for users of a Hiddify Manager server who want to use sing-box instead of the Hiddify App.

This page used to be about the SSH proxy

Older versions of this page showed how to add the Hiddify panel's SSH proxy to sing-box. The SSH proxy service was removed in Hiddify Manager v13, so that part no longer applies. The steps below add your normal Hiddify subscription instead.

Recommended: Hiddify App

The easiest app for a Hiddify server is the free Hiddify App. It is on the App Store. See How to install Hiddify App.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An iPhone or iPad with iOS 15 or later.
  • Your user page link. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal Hiddify page, where your subscription links are.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). The app can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Download the app
docs.text:
The official sing-box app for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV is now called sing-box MT. The old App Store listing (id6451272673) no longer exists.

  • iOS / iPadOS (App Store: sing-box MT)
  • Android (Google Play)
  • Other platforms: see the official sing-box download page.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.
  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap sing-box. If you don't see it, tap View More.
  4. Tap Import To App. The sing-box app opens and asks to add the profile.
  5. Confirm. The new profile now appears in the app's Profiles list.

If the app doesn't open, use the manual way below.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the manual way
docs.text:
1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Hiddify / Singbox and tap Get Link.
  3. Tap Copy Link.

  4. Open the sing-box app and go to the Profiles menu.

    1. Tap New Profile.

    2. Set Type to Remote.

    3. Type any name you like in the Name field.

    4. Paste the link you copied into the URL field.

    5. Tap Create.

      The profile now appears in the list of profiles.

      Note

      The screenshots on this page come from an older version of sing-box. Menu names in the current app may look slightly different.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Go to the Dashboard menu.
  2. Select the profile you added.
  3. Turn on the Enabled switch. If iOS asks to add a VPN configuration, tap Allow.

When it works, the VPN icon appears at the top of your iPhone screen and websites open normally. If it doesn't connect, go back to Profiles, update the profile, and try again. If it still fails, ask your server admin to check your account.

docs.title: Tutorial for Stash app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your Hiddify profile to Stash on iPhone and iPad and how to use its main modes. Stash is a paid app based on Clash.

Recommended: Hiddify App

The easiest app for a Hiddify server is the free Hiddify App. It is on the App Store. See How to install Hiddify App.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Buy and install Stash from the App Store. The App Store lists iOS 16 or later.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal Hiddify page.

In Stash, a profile is a file (in YAML format) that holds all your connections (configs) and the rules for which traffic goes through the VPN.

docs.title: Add your profile: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.
  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap Stash. If you don't see it, tap View More. You can also download the app from here.
  4. Tap Import To App. Stash opens and adds your profile.

If that doesn't work, add the profile by hand as shown below.

Lite and Normal profiles no longer exist

Older versions of the user page had an iOS tab with two Stash profiles: a green Lite profile (only blocked sites go through the VPN) and an orange Normal profile (all traffic goes through the VPN). The current panel offers a single Clash Meta subscription instead. If you want local sites to open without the VPN, ask your admin; this is set on the server.

docs.title: Add your profile by hand
docs.text:
First get the link:

  1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Clash Meta and tap Get Link. A window with a QR code and a Copy Link button opens.

docs.title: Copy the link into Stash
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.
  2. Open Stash. On the Settings page, tap Config File.

  3. Tap Download from URL.

    1. Paste the link and tap Download. The profile is added to the app.

docs.title: Add the profile with a QR code
docs.text:
1. Keep the QR code from the user page on screen (for example on a computer).
  2. Open Stash. On the Settings page, tap Config File.

  3. Tap Download from QRcode.

  4. Scan the QR code. The profile is added to the app.

docs.title: The Policy menu
docs.text:
This menu shows the policies, that is the configs in the profiles you imported.

Each mode in the Policy menu works together with a mode in the Outbound section, which is explained further down.

docs.title: Proxy mode
docs.text: Uses one config that you choose. It is used with the Global outbound mode.

docs.title: Automatic mode
docs.text: The app connects to the config with the best test result. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Sequential mode
docs.text: The app uses the configs one after another, switching from time to time. This spreads the load over time. It is different from load-balance mode, which uses several configs at the same time. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Auto mode
docs.text: The automatic config selection used by Automatic mode.

docs.title: Load-Balance mode
docs.text: Uses several connections at the same time, which spreads the load over them. This can help when the server's IP is partly blocked and single connections work badly. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: Tap the lightning icon to test the connections.

docs.title: Update your profiles
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings, then Config File.
  2. Hold your finger on a profile.
  3. In the menu that appears, tap Update Now.

docs.title: Update your profiles automatically
docs.text:
1. In Settings, tap More Settings.

  2. In the CONFIG FILE section, set the time between updates in Update Interval.

  3. Turn on Auto Update.

Stash also updates your profiles each time you open the app.

docs.title: Choose the Outbound mode
docs.text: On the Home page of the app, the Outbound section has three modes.

docs.title: Rule mode
docs.text: Uses the rules in the profile to decide which traffic goes through the VPN. For example, if the profile has rules for local sites, their traffic does not go through the VPN.

docs.title: Global mode
docs.text: Ignores the rules. You pick one config in the Policy menu under Proxy mode, and all your phone's traffic goes through it. This is useful when you want to use one specific config.

docs.title: Direct mode
docs.text: Nothing goes through the VPN. It is as if the VPN were off.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: Go to Settings, then On Demand.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: When this is on, your VPN is always on.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: When this is on, the VPN is active only while the phone is unlocked and turns off at other times.

docs.title: Troubleshoot connections
docs.text: To see more details about your connections, open the Utilities menu and tap Network Diagnosis. It shows a log of all connections, which helps you find problems. The Connectivity and Proxy subsections are the most useful.

docs.title: Tutorial for Streisand
docs.text: This application is one of the free apps for iOS that can be installed on iOS versions 14 and later.

docs.title: Download the application
docs.text: To install the application, you can download and install it here.

docs.title: Add subscription link
docs.text: There are 2 ways to do this.

docs.title: Copy the subscription link
docs.text:
• For this, go to your user panel and open the section related to auto in the section of All Configs.
  • Now you can Copy the QR code.
  • Enter the software and press the + button.
  • Then the subscription is added to the software and the configurations are loaded.

docs.title: Scan the subscription link
docs.text:
• You can scan the QR code instead of copying the subscription link.
  • Click the + button in the software and click the Scan QRCode option and scan the QR code.
  • Then the subscription is added to the software and the configurations are loaded.

docs.title: Subscription settings
docs.text: To do this, tap and hold on the subscription added to the software. The following options will appear.

docs.title: Latency
docs.text: Calculates the amount of delay related to the configurations.

docs.title: TCP Ping
docs.text: It takes TCP ping test from configs.

docs.title: ICMP Ping
docs.text:
It takes a normal pinning test from the configs.

Note: The difference between normal ping test and TCP ping is in the type of protocol used.

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Use this option to update your subscription.

docs.title: Edit
docs.text: Use this option to edit the subscription link.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: Use this option to delete the subscription.

docs.title: DNS Settings
docs.text: On the main page of the software, there are settings related to DNS, by entering it, you can adjust it and change the server and the type of protocol used.

docs.title: DoH
docs.text: It is a protocol that provides DNS over HTTPS. It means that DNS requests are sent in web format.

docs.title: DoT
docs.text: In this protocol, DNS requests are sent based on the TCP protocol.

docs.title: DoU
docs.text: In this protocol, DNS requests are sent based on the UDP protocol.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: On this page, there are general settings of the software, which will be explained later.

docs.title: Import Configuration
docs.text: Use this option to add the configuration file from the device manually.

docs.title: Export Configuration
docs.text: This option can be used to transfer the imported configuration from the device to another device.

docs.title: Subscription
docs.text: By activating the Update On Open option, the subscription will be updated automatically when the software is opened.

docs.title: Reset
docs.text: In this section, you can reset the settings related to the application.

docs.title: Fragment activation
docs.text:
To activate the fragment on TLS connections, you need to click on the connection on this app and activate the Fragment option. The following parameters are suggested to be specified in the relevant fields.

packets: tlshello

length: 100-200

Interval: 10-20

Depending on the operator, you may need to change the parameters or change the type of packets from tlshello to `tcp segment 1-3'' mode. Of course, this condition may be detected earlier.packets: 1-3`

docs.title: Tutorial for V2Box app
docs.text: This software is a subset of V2ray software that was released for iOS.

docs.title: Add subscription links to the app
docs.text: For this, enter your user panel and use the link for Subscription b64 in the section of All configs.

docs.title: Copy the link
docs.text:
• Click on the button next to the link and click Copy in the opened window.
  • Open the V2Box software and select Configs from the bottom menu.
  • Tap the + button.
  • Select the Add Subscription option.
  • Give a desired name and copy the link copied in the previous step into the URL.
  • Then click Add Subscribe to add the configurations to the program.
  • After that, the program will automatically test the connections.

docs.title: Scan QR code
docs.text:
• To do this, click the button next to the link in the user panel
  • Tap + in the V2Box app.
  • Select the Scan QR option.
  • Then scan the QR code on the user's page with the phone's camera.
  • Configs are automatically added and the connection test is performed from them.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: To do this, click on Ping All in the Configs list so that all configs are tested.

docs.title: Update subscription
docs.text: To do this, press Configs + in the menu, then select Update All Subscriptions. By doing this, all subscriptions will be updated.

docs.title: Automatic update of links
docs.text: To do this, click on the three-line menu at the top of the Configs screen and activate the Auto Update option.

docs.title: Add configs individually
docs.text: Although this method is not recommended and it is not possible to update it, but if necessary, you can click the + button in Configs, then click Import V2ray URL from Clipboard to add the desired configuration to the program.

docs.title: Connect to VPN
docs.text:
To turn on the VPN, go to the Home menu and slide the bottom button to the right.

On this page, general information about the connection, such as the amount of upload and download and the amount of memory used, is displayed.

docs.title: Configuration and advanced settings
docs.text: These guides explain the settings of the Hiddify Manager admin panel: WARP, Reality, the Telegram proxy and bot, backups, updates and more. Choose a guide from the menu.

docs.title: How to Reset HiddifyManager to default
How to Reset HiddifyManager to default
docs.text:
In this article, we are going to teach how to raw the HiddifyManager (complete reset of the panel and database) similar to the initial installation. If you intend to return the Hiddify panel to its initial settings, this tutorial is prepared for you. Follow these steps to the end.

  • To begin, first SSH into your server.

  • Then, by using the combination keys Ctrl+c or selecting the Cancel button, close the Hidیify menu to access the terminal (command line environment) of your server.

  • If after performing these steps, the Hiddify menu is still displayed to you, type the word clear and press enter.

It should be mentioned here that if you need to backup your panel, make a backup of the settings-backup before proceeding. * Then enter this command in the terminal of your server to completely delete the current database:

rm -rf /opt/hiddify-config/hiddifypanel/hiddifypanel.db
* Then open the menu again using the following command:

bash /opt/hiddify-config/menu.sh
  • And select Reinstall option from the Hiddify menu and wait for the panel to be reinstalled.
  • After finishing, you can access the new panel and configure it using the displayed admin links.

In this method, after the re-installation is finished, the panel will be completely retested and similar to the initial installation.

docs.title: How to activate WARP on HiddifyManager
How to activate WARP on the Hiddify panel
docs.text: Many websites, including Google, restrict the access of users through VPN. Because several different connections go from the same IP to Google's server at the same time, this behavior is similar to cyber malicious behavior, and because of this, the connection is disrupted, and Google gives a 403 error, for example. Other websites do not allow communication and use of the service. Here is one way to solve the problem using Cloudflare's WARP service.

docs.title: What is WARP?
docs.text:
Warp is a Cloudflare service that provides secure and encrypted communication over its network. After performing security checks on the target client and making sure there is no malicious behavior, it opens the connection to the Internet. It assigns an IP to that system and communicates through it. In fact, Warp is a tool that hides your server IP from the sites that your users visit. Because the IP of the server is hidden, so access is established.

Warp has several levels of service, the free service of which has a traffic volume limit, and after crossing the limit, access is limited. It is better to use its special service called WARP Plus, which supports high volume. On Hiddify, it is possible to use this version of Warp, which will be explained later on how to activate it.

docs.title: Setting up WARP on Hiddify
docs.text:
Go to the panel settings section, in this section you can see the WARP settings. Open it.

When you deactivate it, you need to give it a Warp Plus code, which you need to get this service from Cloudflare. Of course, to get this code, there are different bots in Telegram that give you this code, but none of them are approved by us.

docs.title: Mode "All"
docs.text: It passes all traffic through the warp, even the sites that don't have problems pass through the warp.

docs.title: Mode "Only blocked and local websites"
docs.text:
Only domestic sites and Google, Spotify, Netflix, Openai, ipinfo.io use Warp.

  • Note: If for any reason there is an error in the inserted code, the warp will be disabled. So make sure to use the code correctly. Select and copy the code provided by the bot correctly and place it in the desired field.

docs.title: How to check if warp is active or not?
docs.text:
To do this, check the Status of the panel from the Actions menu.

The system status is displayed on this page. Also, the status of the warp connection, the IP allocated for the use of the warp traffic is displayed.

  • Note that Warp is always active as a service. That is, here even if you have disabled it in the settings, it will be displayed again.

  • When you disable warp from the settings, traffic will not pass through the service even though it is enabled.

  • If you have entered the limited or unlimited Warp Plus code, the type of service will be displayed as Limited or Unlimited on this page.

You can also use the ipinfo site. If the IP displayed on this page belongs to Cloudflare despite the filter breaker being turned on; In this case, the warp is activated correctly.

You can also use the ip.gs website, and if Cloudflare's IP is displayed, it means that Warp is activated.

docs.title: How to reinstall WARP service?
docs.text:
• To do this, SSH to your server; Press Ctrl+c or click Cancel to exit Hiddify menu.

  • Now run this command.

cd /opt/hiddify-manager/other/warp/wireguard && bash install.sh

docs.title: How to change IP WARP?
docs.text:
• To do this, SSH to your server; Press Ctrl+c or click Cancel to exit Hidify menu.

  • Now run this command.

cd /opt/hiddify-manager/other/warp/wireguard && bash change_ip.sh
  • After that, the assigned IP is changed by Warp. You can see the IP using the method given above.

docs.title: How to backup and restore HiddifyManager
How to backup and restore panel on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
Many times you need to backup the panel and restore it on another server. For example, your server is filtered or there is a problem that you cannot continue on that server. In this case, continue the following steps until the end to learn how to do this. Backup current panel via web

In the admin panel, enter settings and then backup and click on receive backup file.

Here you can specify the storage location of your backup file so that the json file related to the settings is saved.

docs.title: Sending the backup file to Telegram
docs.text: Every 6 hours, the panel automatically backs up for you, and if you have activated the Telegram bot, it will be sent to the bot.

docs.title: Backup during important operations
docs.text:
When updating or reinstalling the panel, it is backed up and you can access and use it.

Note: If for any reason the Telegram bot was not available to you and you were not able to backup via the web, you can access the previous backups of the system from the following path.

/opt/hiddify-manager/hiddify-panel/backup

and then transfer the file to your PC. More info here

docs.title: Restoring backup file
docs.text:
Now install the panel on the new server and do nothing on the Quick-setup page.

Enter the Backup menu in Settings.

Here, select the backup file that you saved in the previous step. Enable recovery options as per your need. For example, if you want to restore the entire panel, select all 3 options and wait for the operation to finish.

docs.title: Changing subdomain settings
docs.text:
Change your subdomain settings to the new server's IP. That is, go wherever you have defined your domains and enter the new IPs. For example, enter the DNS settings in Cloudflare and go to the previously registered records and just change the IP.

The work is done. The panel with the admin link will come up on the new server.

docs.title: How to configure HiddifyManager properly (Getting familiar with its different parts)
How to configure HiddifyManager properly
docs.text:
This page walks you through the first setup of the HiddifyManager admin panel and explains what each part of the panel does. Read it right after you install the panel, or whenever you want to know what a menu or setting is for.

Updated for HiddifyManager v14

Since v13 the panel opens Admin V2 by default, and in v14 the old (classic) admin pages redirect to it. The menu names on this page are the Admin V2 names. Most screenshots below were taken in an older version, so your screen will look different, but the ideas are the same.

The panel makes running proxies easier, but it cannot fix a blocked server or a broken domain. If you finish this page and your users still cannot connect, read Troubleshooting connectivity issues.

There is also a video walkthrough in Persian. It was recorded for an older version.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  1. A server with a clean IP. A clean IP is one that is not blocked in your users' country. Check it with How to make sure the server's IP or domain is clean. If the IP is blocked, get a new IP or a new server.
  2. HiddifyManager installed, as described in the installation guide. At the end of the install you get your admin links. The admin link contains your secret path and your admin ID, so it works like a password. See the correct format of the admin link.
  3. A registered domain that is reachable. A domain is a name such as example.com that points to your server. See domain types and how to register them, then check that the domain is clean.

If a word on this page is new to you, see Basic concepts.

docs.title: Open the admin panel for the first time
docs.text:
• If you used a one-click install link from a provider such as Vultr or OVH, wait about 10 minutes. You then get a one-time link that opens the admin page.
  • If you installed over SSH, the admin links are printed in the terminal at the end of the install. Open one of the Secure (https, domain) links in your browser. Use the IP link only if no domain link works.
  • If you lost the links, connect to your server over SSH and run:
hiddify admin

The first time you open the admin page, the Quick setup wizard starts.

docs.title: Quick setup
docs.text:
The wizard has a few short steps. You can change everything later in Settings.

  1. Welcome: choose the admin panel language and the country your users are in. The country selects settings that suit its filtering.
  2. Password: set a password for the admin area (at least 8 characters).
  3. Domains: point your domain to the server IPs shown on the page (an A record for IPv4, AAAA for IPv6). Then type your domain and press Enter. The panel detects the domain type by itself; tap the type to change it. You need at least one direct, CDN or subscription-only domain.
  4. Protocols: pick the protocols you want to offer. Choose as few as you need.
  5. Nodes (optional): connect other Hiddify servers to manage them from this panel. You can skip this.
  6. Finish: review your choices and click Finish. The panel applies the configuration and reinstalls the services. This takes a few minutes. The log and your new admin links are shown while it runs.

When it finishes, the panel is ready to use. Copy the new admin links and keep them somewhere safe.

docs.title: The admin menu
docs.text:
The Admin V2 sidebar has three groups:

  • Manager: Dashboard, Users, Admins, Broadcast, Nodes and Utils.
  • Settings: Proxy Editor, Domains, Settings, Backup, Actions (the Apply & status page) and, if you set one up, your Telegram bot.
  • Help: links to the tutorials, bug reports and donations.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard shows your server's resources (CPU, RAM, disk, traffic) as charts. If you use several servers (nodes), it also shows the health of each node.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Here you create an account for each person who will use your proxies.

  1. Open Users and click the add button.
  2. Enter a name, the usage limit (in GB), the number of days (package days) and the reset mode.
  3. Save.

Each user has their own user page. Open it from the link next to the user. At the top of the user page the user can download a client app for their device. Further down are the user's configs.

You can give users access in three ways:

  1. The user page link (recommended). The user opens it and finds everything there.
  2. The subscription link. A subscription link is one address that the app re-reads to get the latest configs. If you change your settings, the user's app updates itself.
  3. A single config link. It does not update. If you change your settings, you must send the user a new link.

For help connecting client apps, see the YouTube playlist and the client tutorials on the HiddifyManager tutorials page.

docs.title: Admins
docs.text:
Here you create accounts for other people who help you manage the panel. Click the add button and fill in the form.

There are three admin types:

  • Super admin: full access to the whole panel and all settings.
  • Admin: can manage users and some settings.
  • Agent: can only manage users.

For each admin you can:

  • limit the number of users and active users;
  • allow or forbid adding sub-admins;
  • reset their password.

Note

Each admin's link contains their secret ID. If you change it, that admin's panel address changes completely. See the correct format of the admin link.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
Open Settings → Domains to add or edit your domains. Each domain has a type, which says how users reach your server, and a TLS mode, which says which certificate or disguise it uses.

Domain types:

  • Direct: the domain points straight to your server's IP. If the domain is on Cloudflare, keep the cloud off (DNS only).
  • CDN: the domain goes through a CDN such as Cloudflare (orange cloud on). A CDN is a network of servers that sits between your users and your server, so your server's IP stays hidden.
  • Relay: users connect to another server in between, which forwards the traffic to this one.
  • Subscription only: used only for subscription links, with no proxies.
  • Cloudflare Worker: Cloudflare workers are created for this domain automatically.

TLS modes: Valid TLS (a real certificate issued automatically), Fake, Reality and DNS (DNS tunnel only).

Changed in v13

The old separate types Auto CDN IP, Fake and Reality are no longer domain types. On upgrade, Auto CDN IP domains became CDN domains, and Fake and Reality domains became Direct domains with the Fake or Reality TLS mode.

docs.title: Direct domain
docs.text:
Click the add button and fill in the form.

  • Display name: shown in the users' apps instead of the domain. Use it if you don't want the domain to appear in the configs.
  • Force configs to use these IPs / domains: leave it empty for a direct domain. It is mainly for CDN domains.
  • Show configs of: choose which domains' configs users see when they open their user page through this domain.

docs.title: Subscription-only domain
docs.text:
A subscription-only domain only serves subscription links. Because no proxy traffic goes through it, it is less likely to be blocked, so users can always update their configs.

After you link the subscription-only domain to your connection domains in Show configs of, open a user page through it. The configs on that page use your connection domains.

Tip: a subscription domain works best behind a CDN, so users can still update when your proxy domains are blocked. You can also use a PHP website for subscription links: see How to use a PHP site for sub links.

docs.title: CDN domain
docs.text:
Click the add button and fill in the form.

  • Display name: shown in the users' apps instead of the domain.
  • Force configs to use these IPs / domains: put a clean Cloudflare IP here, or better, a normal DNS record (cloud off) that points to a clean IP. Then, when you need a new clean IP, you only update that DNS record and the panel and configs stay the same. To find clean IPs, see Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP. This field replaces the old Auto CDN IP mode: see Guide for using mode Auto_CDN_IP.
  • Domain fronting: optional. Users' apps show another site's name (SNI) instead of your domain, so a filter only sees that other site. Use sites on the same CDN as your domain. In older versions this was a global setting; now it is set per CDN domain. See Guide for domain fronting.
  • ECH: uses Encrypted Client Hello for this CDN domain. Turn on Enable TLS ECH in Settings first.
  • Show configs of: choose which domains' configs users see on this domain's user page.

If you have many users and want to give each group its own domain, read How to use multi-CDN domains.

docs.title: Other domain setups
docs.text:
• Relay domain: see How to add a relay domain.
  • Fake TLS mode: see How to create and use a fake domain.
  • Reality TLS mode: see How to use Reality.
  • Cloudflare Worker: see How to set up and use Cloudflare workers.

docs.title: Proxies and protocols
docs.text:
You turn protocols on or off in Settings → Settings, in the Proxies Settings group. The Proxy Editor lets advanced users edit each built-in proxy template.

Note: plain HTTP connections are not encrypted. TLS connections are encrypted.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Open Settings → Settings. Common settings are shown first. Click Show advanced settings to see the rest, or use the search box. Settings marked Reinstall only take effect after a reinstall (see Actions). The groups are described below.

docs.title: Admin Settings
docs.text:
• Admin Panel Language: the language of the admin area. Admin V2 is translated into English and Persian; other languages fall back to English.
  • Parent Panel (Multi Server): connect this panel to a central (parent) panel. You then define users on the parent panel, and the usage of all servers is added up there.
  • Node name: a name for this server when it is part of a multi-server setup.

docs.title: Customizing User Page
docs.text:
• User Area Language: the language of the user page.
  • User Page Title: your brand name, shown at the top of the user page.
  • Support Link: a link to your support channel.
  • Support Section Text: a message shown in the support box of the user page.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text:
• Country: the country of your users. It selects settings that suit that country's filtering. Changing it needs a reinstall.
  • Auto Update: lets the panel update itself.
  • Only IPv4: turns off IPv6 on the server.
  • Speed Test: lets users test their connection speed to your server.
  • Decoy Site: a fake website. If someone (for example a filtering system) opens your domain directly, they see this site instead of your panel, which makes your server harder to identify. Do not use bank, payment, Iranian or very famous sites.
  • Firewall: when on, only the ports Hiddify needs (such as 22, 80 and 443) stay open and all other ports are closed.
  • DNS Server, Show Usage in Sublink, Torrent Block and Keep Backups (days) are also here. Keep Backups (days) deletes automatic backups older than this number of days; 0 keeps all of them.

docs.title: Proxies Settings
docs.text:
• Block Domestic Sites: blocks traffic from your server to Iranian sites and .ir domains. This makes it harder for the filtering system to identify your server. We recommend turning it on.
  • Shared Secret: a password used by connections whose traffic is not counted per user.
  • On/off switches for protocols and transports, for example VLess, Trojan, VMess, Reality, Websocket, gRPC, HTTPUpgrade, XHTTP, TCP, QUIC, Naive, AnyTLS, Snell and SOCKS.

Tip: in the Hiddify app, routing rules can send traffic for Iranian sites directly, without the proxy. This saves your server's traffic.

Removed settings

The old V2Ray switch is gone. The browser fingerprint setting (uTLS) is now under Advanced Settings.

docs.title: Domain fronting
docs.text: The old global Domain Fronting settings group was removed. Domain fronting is now set on each CDN domain (see CDN domain). More information: Guide for domain fronting.

docs.title: Telegram Configs
docs.text:
A Telegram proxy works only inside the Telegram app and helps users bypass Telegram filtering.

  • MTProxy FakeTLS Enable: turns the Telegram proxy on or off.
  • Telegram Web Proxy Enable: turns on the Telegram web proxy.
  • Telegram AD Tag: an advertising tag that shows your channel in the user's Telegram chat list.
  • Telegram Fake Domain: a domain whose name is used to disguise the proxy traffic.
  • Telegram Bot Token: connects the panel to your Telegram bot. See How to set up and use the Telegram bot.

Changed in v14

The Telegram proxy now always uses telemt. The old choice of Telegram proxy library (Python, Erlang and others) was removed.

docs.title: HTTP Configuration
docs.text:
• Allow HTTP Connection: allows unencrypted HTTP connections. We don't recommend turning it on.

The custom HTTP port list was removed in v14. Proxies are served on ports 80 and 443 whenever possible.

docs.title: TLS Settings
docs.text:
• Certificate (ACME) Email: the email used when the panel requests certificates.
  • Enable TLS ECH: turns on Encrypted Client Hello support. You then enable it per CDN domain.
  • Allow Invalid SNI.

The custom TLS port list was removed in v14. Since v14 the panel issues and stores certificates itself.

The TLS Trick group (TLS fragment, mixed SNI case, padding) is explained in How the TLS trick works.

docs.title: Shadowsocks
docs.text:
Shadowsocks FakeTLS is a simple disguise that wraps data in TLS-looking packets to fool the filter.

  • Shadowsocks 2022: turns Shadowsocks 2022 on or off.
  • Shadowsocks FakeTLS (Simple OBFS): we don't recommend it.
  • SS FakeTLS FakeDomain: the fake domain used to disguise the packets.

docs.title: ShadowTLS
docs.text:
ShadowTLS shows the firewall a real TLS handshake with a valid certificate from a site you choose. Its switch and fake domain are in the Shadowsocks group.

Warning

The ShadowTLS service was removed from HiddifyManager in v13. Whether ShadowTLS configs still work is not confirmed, so don't rely on it.

docs.title: Advanced Settings
docs.text:
These settings are for experienced users.

  • Package Update Mode: choose Release (stable) or Beta updates.
  • Common Proxy Core: which engine serves the shared proxies: xray, hiddify_core or both. It replaces the old Core setting.
  • uTLS: which browser fingerprint the configs imitate (for example Chrome, Firefox, Safari, iOS or Android).

The parent panel link and the Telegram bot token moved to Admin Settings and Telegram Configs.

docs.title: Very Advanced Settings
docs.text:
• Proxy Path for Admins and Proxy Path for Clients: the secret paths in your admin and user links. They hide your panel and connections from the filter. The panel sets them for you; change them only if you need to. If you change the admin path, your admin link changes.
  • Cloudflare API.

The per-protocol path settings were hidden in v13.

docs.title: WARP and Reality
docs.text:
• WARP: see How to activate WARP.
  • Reality: see How to use Reality.

docs.title: SSH Proxy
docs.text: The SSH proxy service was removed in v13 and is no longer installed, even though its settings group may still appear. See SSH proxy setting.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Open Settings → Backup to make a backup of your panel or restore one.

  • Download backup saves everything in one .json file: settings, users, admins, domains, proxies and certificates. Keep the file safe: it contains passwords and private keys.
  • The panel also makes automatic backups on the server every 6 hours. They are listed under Backups on the server. If your Telegram bot is connected, each one is also sent to you on Telegram.
  • When you restore, you choose which parts to bring back: Settings, Users and Domains.

Details: How to back up and restore.

docs.title: Telegram bot
docs.text: To set up and use the panel's Telegram bot, see How to set up and use the Telegram bot.

docs.title: Actions (Apply & status)
docs.text: Open Settings → Actions. The Apply & status page lets you put changes into effect, update the server and see how everything is doing. Each action shows its log while it runs. You can leave the page; the action keeps running on the server.

docs.title: Check status
docs.text: Shows whether each service is running, plus the server's public IP and WARP. It changes nothing.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: The Logs section lists what each action did. Click View to read a log.

docs.title: Apply changes
docs.text:
Puts your settings, users and domain changes into effect. It is quick, and it is the usual choice after you change something.

  • When it finishes, the page shows your admin links on your domains. They may have changed, so copy them before you leave.
  • If the panel no longer opens after a change, connect to your server over SSH and run hiddify admin to see your current admin links:
hiddify admin
  • If that does not help, see How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH.

docs.title: Update Hiddify
docs.text: Downloads and installs the latest version, then applies it. It takes a while, and the panel restarts at the end. See How to update HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Reinstall
docs.text: Installs everything again and rebuilds all services. Your users and links are not changed. Use it when Apply changes is not enough, for example after you change the panel path, protocols or a setting marked Reinstall. Connections may drop for a few minutes.

docs.title: Restart services
docs.text: Restarts all Hiddify services without reinstalling anything. It is a good first try when something misbehaves. Connections drop for a moment.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: All tutorials and videos are listed on the HiddifyManager tutorials page.

docs.title: How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH (Working with Hiddify Menu)
docs.text:
Windows 10 and 11 usually already include the SSH client. If the ssh command does not work in PowerShell, install it like this:

  1. Open the Start menu and search for PowerShell.

  2. Right-click PowerShell and choose Run as Administrator.

  3. Run this command in PowerShell:

    Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client

  4. When it finishes, you should see something like this:

The SSH client is now installed.

docs.title: How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH
docs.text:
This page shows you how to manage Hiddify Manager from your server's command line when the web panel does not open, or when you have lost your admin link. It also explains each option of the Hiddify menu.

SSH is a secure way to open a text terminal on your server from your own computer or phone. Everything you type runs on the server.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your server's IP address.
  • The server's username (usually root) and password or SSH key. Your server provider gives you these.
  • An SSH app on your device:
    • Android: Termius
    • Windows: PowerShell (or PuTTY)
    • macOS: Terminal
    • Linux: Terminal

For a full guide, see How to connect to the server via SSH.

docs.title: Connect to the server
docs.text:
1. Open your SSH app.

  2. Run this command on your device. Replace user with your username and <IP_Address> with your server's IP:

    ssh user@<IP_Address>

    For example, if your username is root and your server's IP is 1.1.1.1:

    ssh root@1.1.1.1

  3. Type yes if you are asked to trust the server, then enter your password. (The password is not shown while you type. This is normal.)

If the connection works, you see the server's command prompt, and the Hiddify menu may open by itself.

Password login warning

If password login is enabled on your server, the menu first shows a WARNING that your server is open to abuse. Press Enter to continue. To fix it, follow Disable SSH password authentication.

docs.title: Open the Hiddify menu
docs.text:
Run this command on your server to open the Hiddify menu:

hiddify

The menu looks like this (the screenshots on this page are from an older version, so some items may look a little different):

Use the arrow keys to move, and press Enter to choose an item. The sections below explain each item.

Commands instead of the menu

Most menu items are also available as direct commands, for example hiddify status, hiddify admin, hiddify restart, hiddify apply and hiddify upgrade release. Run hiddify --help to see them all.

docs.title: Cancel or Quit
docs.text:
Choose Quit (or press Cancel / Esc) to leave the menu and go back to the normal server terminal.

To open the menu again, run this command on your server:

hiddify

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
